documents.title: FOR MEMBER PARTICIPATION IN A COOPERATIVE PRICING SYSTEM

pages.text: 261-11 November 1, 2011 RESOLUTION FOR MEMBER PARTICIPATION IN A COOPERATIVE PRICING SYSTEM WHEREAS, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-11(5) authorizes contracting units to establish a Cooperative Pricing System and to enter into Cooperative Pricing Agreements for its administration; and WHEREAS , the Cranford Police Cooperative Pricing System (ID#47-CPCPS), hereinafter referred to as the “Lead Agency” has offered voluntary participation in a Cooperative Pricing System for the purchase of goods and services; and WHEREAS , on November 1, 2011 the governing body of the Township of West Orange, County of Essex, State of New Jersey duly considered participation in a cooperative Pricing System for the provision and performance of goods and services. NOW BE IT RESOLVED , that this resolution shall be known and may be cited as the Cooperative Pricing Resolution of the Township of West Orange. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED , pursuant to the provisions of N.J.S.A. 40A:11-11(5), the Chief Financial Officer is hereby authorized to enter into a Cooperative Pricing Agreement with the Lead Agency. The Lead Agency shall be responsible for complying with the provisions of the Local Public Contracts Law (N.J.S.A. 40A:11-1 et seq.) and all other provisions of the revised statutes of the State of New Jersey. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Patricia Spango , Council President Adopted: November 1, 2011

documents.title: BINDING THE T OWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE TO PURCHASE ELECTRIC GENERATION SERVICES THROUGH THE ESSEX COUNTY AGGREGATE ENERGY PROCUREMENT COOPERATIVE PRICING SYSTEM ( “ ECAEPC ” ) Bid Cooperative Pricing System ID# 198ECAEPC

pages.text: 260-11 November 1, 2011 A RESOLUTION BINDING THE T OWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE TO PURCHASE ELECTRIC GENERATION SERVICES THROUGH THE ESSEX COUNTY AGGREGATE ENERGY PROCUREMENT COOPERATIVE PRICING SYSTEM ( “ ECAEPC ” ) Bid Cooperative Pricing System ID# 198ECAEPC WHEREAS, the Essex County Aggregate Energy Procurement Cooperative ( hereinafter referred to as “ ECAEPC ”), will from time to time during the Effective Period as defined below solicit bids from electric power suppliers for electri c generation services through an energy aggregation program in which the County of Essex will act as Lead Agency of the ECAEPC, Cooperative Pricing System # 198ECAEPC in accordance with the “ Local Publ ic Contracts Law”, N.J.S.A . 40A:11-10.3 , and the Electric Discount and Energy Competition Act , N.J.S.A. 48: 3-91.3 ( “EDECA” ) and the regulations promulgated there under ; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange is a Participating member of the E CCPS Cooperative Pricing System and is eligible thereby to obtain electric generation services for its own use through one or more contract s to be awarded to electric power suppliers following said bid s for electric generation services pursuant to the aggregation program; and WHEREAS , the Lead Agency will from time to time during the Effective Period December 01, 2011 through November 30, 2013 hereinafter referred to as “Effective Period”) issue one or more Request s for Bids for electric generation services on behalf of the ECAEPC pursuant to the Local Public Contracts Law and EDECA ; and WHEREAS, due to significant volatility and the potential for price increases in the wholesale electric market, Participating Members will preauthorize the Lead Agency to award contract s for Electric Generation Service i n each bid group to one or more electric power suppliers that submit bids which are reasonably forecasted to provide estimated savings to the Participating Member based upon its previous electric usage and utility provided Basic Generation Service rates ; and WHEREAS, the Lead Agency will only award contracts for said electric generation services to electric power suppliers that submit bids with pricing r easonably estimated to be lower than the utility-provided basic generation service; and WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange agrees to purchase all electric power needed for its own use (ex c lusive of on-site electric generation sources) during the Effective Period through any electric power supplier(s) awarded a contract , it being understood that the term of any one contract shall be subject to the provisions of Local Public Contract s Law; and WHEREAS , the Lead Agency will notify the Department of Community Affairs ’ Division of Local Government Services by mail prior to the issuance a Request for Bids for electric generation services , with the understanding that if the Division of Lo c al Government Services does not respond within 10 business days, it will be deemed to have approved the issuance of the Request for Bids or the Request for Rebids . NOW , BE IT RESOLVED that the Township of West Orange binds itself to the ECAEPC, Cooperative Pricing System # 198ECAEPC to purchase all electric power needed for its own use (exclusive of on-site electric generation sources) during the Effective Period from the electric power supplier or suppliers award ed a contract for electric generation services by the Lead Agency . BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Lead Agency of the ECAEPC Cooperative Pricing System is hereby authorized to execute a master performance agreement that obligates the Township of West Orange to purchase electricity at the terms and conditions stated therein with a third-party supplier or suppliers who have been awarded the contract or contracts by the Lead Agency on behalf of the participating members of the ECAEPC Cooperative Pricing System #198ECAEPC , and provided further that all such contracts shall be at prices reasonably forecast and estimated by the Lead Agency to provide savings to the Township of West Orange relative to the price charged for basic generation service by the electric public utility that would otherwise provide such service . BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that ECAEPC is authorized to continue to bid to obtain electric

generation services at any time during the Effective Period on behalf of the ECAEPC Cooperative Pricing System including, for example, a rebid if energy market conditions do not initially lead to a successful bid, on additional dates to be determined by the Lead Agency . BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this Resolution shall take effect immediately upon passage. The authoriz a tion provided to the County of Essex pursuant to the Local Public Contracts Laws (N.J.S.A. 40A : 11-11(5)), Administrative Code N.J.A.C. 14:4-6.4 shall be valid until November 30, 2013 at which time the Cooperative Pricing System will be subject to renew al . Any rescission or expiration of this resolution shall not affect any Agreements entered into prior to such re s cission or expiration . Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Patricia Spango , Council President Adopted: November 1, 2011

252-11 October 25, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 provides for substantial federal funds being made to certain urban communities for use therein through the Community Development Block Grant (“CDBG”) Entitlement Program; and WHEREAS, the Emergency Shelters Grants Program (“ESG”) provided through Subtitle B of Title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (the “Act”) permits for substantial federal funds allocated to prevent homelessness and to enable homeless individuals and families to move toward independent living; and WHEREAS, the Act establishes certain criteria which must be met in order for a county to be recipient of said funding; and WHEREAS, the Interlocal Services Act, N.J.S.A. 40:8A-1 et seq., provides a mechanism through which counties and municipalities may enter into agreements for the provision of joint services; and WHEREAS, the County of Essex and the Township of West Orange wish to enter into a Cooperation Agreement that establishes a legal mechanism through which the county government may apply for, receive, and disburse federal funds available to establish urban counties under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act, the CDBG Entitlement Program, and Title II of the Cranston -Gonzalez National Affordable Housing Act of 1990 (“NAHA”), the HOME Program, to undertake or assist in the undertaking such actions in cooperation with the participating municipalities as may be necessary to participate in the benefits of these programs; and WHEREAS, this Cooperation Agreement shall cover activities with the annual CDBG funds from the Federal Fiscal Years 2012, 2013, and 2014 appropriations and for successive three (3) year periods or until terminated; and WHEREAS , annexed hereto is the Cooperation Agreement to be executed by and between the County of Essex and the Township of West Orange for conducting certain community development activities; NOW, THERFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that the Mayor and Township Clerk be and hereby are respectively authorized to execute and attest to the Cooperation Agreement between the County of Essex for Conducting Certain Community Development Activities. Patricia Spango, Council President K aren J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Adopted: October 25, 2011

pages.text: 24 3 -11 October 11, 2011 2011 ASSISTANCE TO FIREFIGHTERS GRANT (AFG) VEHICLE ACQUISITION PROGRAM RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange in the County of Essex, hereby desires to apply to the Department of Homeland Security’s Federal Emergency Management Agency for funding through its Assistance to Firefighters Grant – Vehicle Acquisition Program to purchase a new pumper to replace a 27-ye ar-old pumper. If awarded, funds will cover travel expenses necessary for pre-construction and final inspection meetings as well as equipment necessary to bring the new pumper into compliance with NFPA standards; and WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange hereby acknowledges that its current 1984 Pirsch open-cab configured vehicle does not meet NFPA standards and that the new apparatus will increase the Township’ s efforts to improve firefighte r and civilian safety, provide incident stabilization, and conserve property. Should the Township be awarded the new vehicle, it will be assigned to the oldest, most densely populated area of the Township. BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED THAT THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE does hereby consent to the authorization of the DHS AFG vehicle application and any other necessary documents in connection therewith. It is understood that if awarded the grant in the amount of approximately $630,132.00, the Township of West Orange will be responsible for a 10% cash match in the amount of $63,014.00. Karen J. 220-11 September 13, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , a personnel matter has arisen within the Police Department; and WHEREAS , the personnel matter emanated, in part, from documentary evidence obtained during certain civil legal proceedings which have been pending for some time; and WHEREAS , it was appropriate to issue a N otice of D isciplinary A ction ; and WHEREAS , Ken Rosenberg, Esq. of Fox Rothschild has handled various disciplinary matters for the Township; and WHEREAS , the charges are based upon the record in the civil proceeding ; and WHEREAS , the former employee attempted to retain a temporary restraining order concerning the prosecution of the charges; and WHEREAS , the Honorable Michael Casale, Judge of the Superior Court, denied the temporary restraining order and set the matter down for a further hearing in October 2011; and WHEREAS , the employee requested a departmental hearing; and WHEREAS , the Township has previously utilized the services of hearing officer Ellen O'Connell, Esq. with regard to various previous matters; and WHEREAS , the Departmental hearings were conducted on August 17, 2011 and August 24, 2011 and post hearing submissions were submitted on September 7, 2011; and WHEREAS , the Township's Law Department recommends the allocation of funds in order to finalize the hearing and represent the Township's interests; and NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that Ellen O'Connell, Esq. be and is retained as the hearing officer at a rate of $150 per hour up to a maximum of $7,500; and be it further RESOLVED , that Ken Rosenberg, Esq. of Fox Rothschild be and is hereby

retained as the Township's special counsel at a rate of $150 per hour not to exceed $15,000; and be it further RESOLVED , that a copy of this Resolution shall be made available to the public and published in accordance with applicable law. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Patricia Spango, Council President Adopted: September 13, 2011 I hereby certify funds are available from: Account No. Chief Financial Officer

219-11 September 13, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange (the “Township”) is the owner of real property known as Block 170, Lots 13, 15.03 and 17 on the Tax Map of the Township commonly known as 590 Mt. Pleasant Avenue; and WHEREAS, the Township utilizes this property as an integral part of its Recycling Program; and WHEREAS , the operations conducted here include the composting of leaves, the processing of vegetative wood waste and operating a recycling convenience center for West Orange residents for mixed paper, cardboard, and commingled containers; and WHEREAS , the Township requires the services of a firm to operate the Recycling Center for Class B materials, exempt wood, Class C materials, exempt compost and to operate the Recycling Center for mixed paper, cardboard and commingled containers; and WHEREAS , in July 2008, the Township utilizing the competitive contracting provisions of the Local Public Contracts Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-4.1 through 4.5, advertised a Request for Proposal (“RFP”) entitled “Operation of the Township of West Orange Recycling Center for Class B, Exempt Woods, Class C Exempt Compost Operation and the Recycling Convenience Center” in order to enter into a Contract to operate the West Orange Recycling Center (the “Contract”) and WHEREAS , the RFP sought proposals for a term of three (3) years with two (2) one- year options; and WHEREAS , the Township received a single proposal in response to the RFP from Reliable Wood Products, LLC (“Reliable Wood”) of One Caven Point Road, Jersey City, New Jersey, 07305, a copy of the proposal is annexed hereto as Attachment “A;” and WHEREAS , the Director of Public Works determined that Reliable Wood’s proposal

was responsive and compliant to the specifications contained within the Township’s RFP; and WHEREAS , an evaluation committee was formed to review and discuss the Proposal submitted by Reliable Wood and each members was tasked with individually evaluating the Proposal based on the criteria in the RFP; and WHEREAS , following the recommendation of the evaluation committee to award the Contract to Reliable Wood and the Business Administrator’s concurrence with the evaluation committee’s recommendations, the Township Council issued a resolution awarding the Contract to Reliable Wood, annexed hereto as Attachment “B,” and WHEREAS , Reliable Wood and the Township executed a Management, Operation and Maintenance Service Agreement for the West Orange Recycling Center and Composting Facility, annexed hereto as Attachment “C;” and WHEREAS , the Contract provided that Reliable Wood would pay rent in the amount of $7,500 per month ($90,000 per year) to the Township; and WHEREAS , the Contract commenced on October 1, 2008; and WHEREAS , the initial term of the Contract is set to expire on September 30, 2011; and WHEREAS , Reliable Wood has perform in a satisfactory manner and should continue for an additional one year extension as set forth in the Contract .

NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE that the Mayor is hereby authorized to issue a one-year extension to Reliable Wood as set forth in the Contract under the terms set forth in the Contract and proposal submitted by Reliable Wood. Karen J. 215 -11 August 30, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , there exists in the Township of West Orange, a need for the services of a firm or individual specializing in the investigation, research, planning, preparation and pursuit of grants and other programs submitted to various County, State and Federal authorities and foundations for obtaining vital financial and other aid for municipal programs; and WHEREAS, such services involve professional knowledge and services as financial advisors pertaining to grants as well as specialized knowledge of available County, State and Federal aid programs and corporate and private foundations and the preparation of applications, submissions and actions necessary to obtain and successfully pursue such programs ; and WHEREAS, the need for such services is great and immediate and the necessary funds are available; and WHEREAS, Alicia Skinner, trading as Skinner Consulting Services, has served as the Township’s Grant Writer since 2007 ; and WHEREAS , the Township seeks to re-appoint Alicia Skinner as the Township’s Grant Writer for an additional six (6) month period at the rate of $14,000, commencing September 1, 2011 and ending February 29, 2012 ; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by Township Council of the Township of West Orange, New Jersey as follows: 1. The contract for the performance of all necessary professional consultation and work involved in the study of County, State, Federal corporate and private aid funds needs of the Township of West Orange, New Jersey, and the related research, planning, preparation, submission and proceeding with all applications and programs for such programs is hereby awarded to Alicia Skinner. Alicia Skinner agrees that new grants (“New Grants”) of at least the amount paid to it will be obtained during the term of this agreement and agrees that it will continue to provide services beyond the term of this agreement at no cost until New

2 Grants exceeding the amount received are awarded. This amount specifically excludes all currently existing grants. 2. Reimbursement of Expenses. Alicia Skinner shall receive reimbursement for out- of-pocket expenses up to a maximum of $50 per month during the contract period upon submission of receipts for necessary and approved supplies including ink cartridges, postage and related items. 3. Independent Contractor. Alicia Skinner is an independent contractor who shall be solely responsible for her own work hours and daily responsibilities. As an independent contractor, Alicia Skinner shall be fully responsible for all obligations to any taxing authority or other governmental entity. Alicia Skinner shall receive no monetary or other benefits not specifically enumerated in this agreement. 4. New Grants. New Grants shall be defined as receipt of monies not previously received by the Township during the past five (5) years. 5. All grant applications are subject to the approval of the Township in its sole discretion. No grant application shall be submitted without the approval of the Township Council. 6. Reporting. Alicia Skinner shall submit a written report to the Mayor and Council concerning all services rendered and new grants obtained on a quarterly basis. In addition, Alicia Skinner shall attend any meetings requested by the Mayor and/or Business Administrator to discuss potential grants and report as to timetables for submission of grant applications, status of grant applications, and areas of available grant funds. 7. Alicia Skinner shall be paid for the services set forth in this agreement the sum of $2,333.33 per month effective September 1, 2011 and continuing each month thereafter with the Township and Alicia Skinner having the right to terminate this agreement on five (5) days written notice at any time . 8. A copy of this Resolution shall be published in accordance with the law.

3 9. A copy of the Resolution shall be maintained on file with the Municipal Clerk available for public inspection. Karen J. 214-11 August 30, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange is the owner of unimproved and undeveloped real property in Blocks 176.04 and 176.08 along Arnold Terrace an unimproved street; and WHEREAS, this property is located behind residential properties along Cliff Street in the Grande at Pleasantdale subdivision; and WHEREAS, the property owners at 26 Cliff Street, Maurice and Ertha McKenzie, and 28 Cliff Street, Marc and Laura Shaprio, expressed an interest in purchasing a portion of T ownship owned property to buffer their residences from any future development of Township property; and WHEREAS, the size of the parcels both the McKenzie’s and the Shaprio's expressed an interest to acquire exceeded the minimum required lot areas for properties in an R-5 residential zone which is 10,000 square feet; and WHEREAS, to protect the two parcels from any future development and to preserve the land in its current wooded condition the Township will place deed restrictions on the parcels and conservation easements within them; and WHEREAS, these restrictions make these parcels non buildable and thus they may be offered for sale to adjoining lot owners in lieu of a public auction ; and WHEREAS, the Township obtained the Professional Land Surveying services of G.C. Stewart Associates, Inc. of Essex Fells, New Jersey to perform a boundary survey of Township owned property in Blocks 176.04, 176.07 and 176.08 which are adjacent to the rear yards of properties fronting Cliff Street; and WHEREA S, based on the boundary survey, Charles P. Stewart, P.L.S. of G.C. Stewart Associates prepared a plan entitled Map Showing Proposed Land Merger, Block 176.07, 176.08, Block 176.04, Marmon Terrace and Arnold Terrace dated May 7, 200 8 which created two parcels- one adjacent to property of the Mackenzie’s consisting of Block 176.08, Filed Map Lots 11, 12 and a portion of Fi led Map Lot 13 containing 14,008 square feet and a second parcel adjacent to property of the Shaprio’s c onsisting of Block 176.04, Filed Map Lots 17 and 18 and a portion of Arnold Terrace to be vacated containing 22,321 square feet; and WHEREAS, since the parcels are not buildable lots the Township Assessor placed a value of $1.00 per s quare foot on them or $14,008.00 and $22,321.00 respectively; and WHEREAS, all adjoining property owners were notified of the sale of these parcels at the values stated with deed restrictions which would prohibit building on the se parcels and conservation easements to maintain them in their current conditions; and

WHEREAS, only the Mackenzie’s of 26 Cliff Street, Block 178.56, Lot 12 expressed an interest to purchase the proposed 14,008 square foot parcel adjacent to their property and only the Shaprio’s of 28 Cliff Street, Block 178.56, Lot 11 expressed an interest to purchase the proposed 22,321 square foot parcel adjacent to their property; and WHEREAS, based on the interest of the MacKenzies and the Shaprios the Township’ s Administration recommends selling the parcels of Township owned property adjacent to their residences as depicted on the Map Showing Proposed Land Merger prepared by Charles P. Stewart, P.L.S. to them with restrictions preventing any building and with conservation easemen ts to preserve the land in its current condition at a consideration of $1.00 per square foot or $14,008.00 and $22,321.00 respectively; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that it concurs with the recommendation of the Township Administration to sell Township owned property as depicted on the Map Showing Prepared Land Merger, Block 17 6.07, Block 176.08, Block 176.04 Marmon Terrace and Arnold Terrace prepared by Charles P. Stewart, P.L.S. dated May 7, 2008 consisting of 14,008 square feet in Block 176.08 to the adjoin in g property owner Maurice and Ertha McKenzie of 26 Cliff Street and to sell Township owned property consisting of 22,321 square feet in Block 176.04 and a portion of vacated Arnold Terrace to the adjoining property owner Marc and Lauren Shaprio of 28 Cliff Street with deed restrictions to prohibit any building on each lot and conservation easements to prohibit disturbance of the parcels and to maintain them in their current condition at a consideration of $1.00 per square foot or $14,008.00 and $23,321.00 respectively. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Admini stration is directed to prepare all necessary Ordinances to authorize the sale and Ordinances to vacate a portion of Arnold Terrace. ________________________________ _____________________________ Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Patricia Spango, Council President Adopted: August 30, 2011

213-11 August 30, 2011 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, on February 17, 2011 the Township of West Orange advertised for bids for the project entitled “2010 Roadway Improvements-Phase I Various Streets”, prepared by the Engineering Division for the Township; and WHEREAS, the Township on March 15, 2011 received 19 bids for this project; and WHEREAS, on March 29, 2011 the Township Council by Resolution No. 63-11 awarded a contract for this project to the lowest responsive bidder, A & J Contractor’s Group, 105 Federal Road, Monroe Township, New Jersey in the amount of $512,777.30 of which $437,000 was funded by Community Development Block Grants; and WHEREAS, the bid and contract were based on unit prices; and WHEREAS, the streets in this project included Central Place, Glebe Street, Cary Street, Lafayette Street, portions of Chestnut Street and Cherry Street and all of Franklin Avenue; and WHEREAS, A & J Contractor’s Group, Inc. proceeded with the improvements associated with this project; and WHEREAS, as the work neared completion the Engineering Division determined it significantly underestimated the quantities of work on a portion of Franklin Avenue between Chestnut Street and the Montclair line; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated June 1, 2011 restated the estimated quantities of six major items of construction omitted from the original bid quantity estimate; and WHEREAS, those additional bid quantities as well as a supplemental item for culvert repair on Central Place were stated in Change Order No. 1 dated June 1, 2011 for this project totaling $90,000.00; and WHEREAS, the Township Council by Resolution No. 139-11 dated June 14, 2011 approved Change Order No. 1; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated June 1, 2011 indicated a final

Change Order reflecting as built quantities would be submitted for approval; and WHEREAS, Change Order No. 2 and Final reflects the final as-built quantities and the final project cost of $649,540.04 or an increase of $46,762.74 over the previously authorized amount through Change Order No. 1 of $602,777.30; and WHEREAS, subsequent to the approval of Change Order No. 1 the Township received additional contingency funding of $50,500 from the Community Development Block Grant Program bringing the total available funds to $653,277.30 or $3,737.26 more than the final contract amount; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated August 23, 2011 recommends Change Order No. 2 and Final for this project be approved which represents a 7.7 percent increase over the amount of $602,777.30 previously authorized and a 26.7 percent increase over original contract amount; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that Change Order No. 2 and Final in the amount of $46,762.74 for the project 2010 Roadway Improvements-Phase I, Various Streets with A & J Contractor’s Group, Monroe Township, New Jersey be approved bringing the final contract amount to $649,540.04 or a 7.7 percent increase in the amount previously authorized and 26.7 percent higher than the original award amount. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that $3,737.26 previously authorized under Change Order No. 1 be returned to the Capital Improvement Fund for future roadway projects. KAREN J. CARNEVALE, MUNICIPAL CLERK PATRICIA SPANGO, COUNCIL PRESIDENT I her e by certify contingency funds are available in the amount of $50,500 from the Community Development Block Grant Program contingent upon the execution of an amended contract for this project and the issuance of a Purchase Order by the County. _______________________________________________ CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

208-11 August 30, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange Police Department desires to enter into a Shared Service Agreement with the County of Essex for the purpose of sharing law enforcement services and information by being permitted access to the County Wide Criminal Justice Information System Network (“CJIS”), which allows for the connectivity of a municipal police department to the County via a private IP Network; and WHEREAS, the routers provided as part of this Shared Service Agreement will be configured to encrypt New Jersey State Police Criminal Justice Information System transmissions, Integrated Law Enforcement Initiative (“ILEI”) transmissions and other traffic as identified by the ILEI governing committee; and WHEREAS, under the Shared Service Agreement the Township of West Orange agrees to pay the County of Essex an annual fee of $15,000 per line for the right to participate in the CJIS; and WHEREAS, this annual fee includes the following services: 1. Recurring line charges and managed network services fees paid by the County of Essex to Verizon Business Network Services, Inc.; 2. Annual maintenance fees for the ILEI solution paid by the County to Enforsys, Inc.; 3. Annual maintenance fees for the Fingerprint Store and Forward solution paid by the County to Clearview Data Systems, Inc.; 4. Annual maintenance fees for the equipment and system software; and 5. System administrator support services; and WHEREAS, this Shared Service Agreement shall become effective upon signing and shall terminate on February 28, 2015, unless terminated prior by either the municipality upon ninety (90) days written notice or by the County upon thirty (30) days written notice; and WHEREAS, in order to gain access to the CJIS all municipal law enforcement agencies must agree to all terms of the Memorandum of Understanding for Contribution of Data into the New Jersey Data Exchange previously entered into between the New Jersey Department of Law and Public Safety, Division of State Police, Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness and the Essex County Sheriff; and WHEREAS, annexed hereto is a copy of the Shared Services Agreement and the Memorandum of Agreement between the County of Essex and the Participating Law Enforcement Agencies within the County of Essex to Create and Participate in the Essex County “Integrated Law Enforcement Initiative”; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, County of Essex and State of New Jersey, that the Mayor and Township Clerk are authorized to execute and attest to, respectively, the annexed Shared Services Agreement for County-Wide Criminal Justice Information System Network Agreement with the County of Essex and the Memorandum of Agreement between the County of Essex and the Participating Law Enforcement Agencies within the County of Essex to Create and Participate in the Essex County “Integrated Law Enforcement Initiative; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a copy of this Resolution be maintained in the Office of the Clerk and published as required by law. Karen J. Carnevale Pat ricia Spango Municipal Clerk Council President Adopted: August 30, 2011

206-11 August 30, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township from time to time permits certain financial advisors and related personnel to provide information to the Township employees concerning deferred compensation p lan s ; and WHEREAS, MetLife Resources ("MLR"), a division of Metropolitan Life Insurance Company ("MetLife"), is a well known and respected company which desires to provide a presentation and platform for Township employees to consider MLR's Deferred Compensation Plan in their sole discretion and at no cost to the Township; and WHEREAS, the Township does not endorse MLR or MetLife by permitting these presentations to Township employees ; and WHEREAS, the Township employees are free to make any determination with regard to their salary, retirement, or other benefits; and WHEREAS, the proposal and offering of the MLR Deferred Compensation Plan is a purely voluntary decision by the Township's employees; and WHEREAS, the implementation of the MLR Deferred Compensation Plan is pursuant to N.J.A.C. 5:37-5.2 and N.J.A.C. 5:37-5.3; and WHEREAS, the implementation of the MLR Deferred Compensation Plan serves the following purposes: (i) desire to attract and retain qualified employees; (ii) accrual of tax benefits to eligible employees through participation in a deferred compensation plan as established pursuant to Section 457(b) of the Internal Revenue Code; (iii) there is no cost to the Township to adopt and implement the deferred compensation plan; and (iv) the implementation of the deferred compensation plan will serve the interests of the Township by enabling the Township to provide enhanced retirement security to its eligible employees; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that pursuant to N.J.A.C. 5:37-5.2, MLR is designated as an additional provider of a deferred compensation plan which may be presented to Township employees at no cost or

2 expense to the Township ; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Township is adopting a deferred compensation plan substantially similar to the one on which a favorable private letter ruling has previously been obtained from the Internal Revenue Services except for the provisions added by the Small Business Job Protection Act of 1996 (U.S. Public Law No. 104-188) and the Economic Growth and Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2001 (U.S. Public Law No. 107-16) and all such provisions are stated in the Plan in terms substantially similar to the text of those provisions of the Internal Revenue Code Section 457. The use of the IRS Ruling is for guidance purposes only and is not precedential ; and it is further RESOLVED , that the Township Chief Financial Officer is designated as the local plan administrator for the administration of the MLR Deferred Compensation P lan; and it is further RESOLVED, that based upon the information available and disclosed by MLR/MetLife, there is no collusion or appearance of collusion between any local official and representative of MLR/Met Life in the selection of MLR pursuant to N.J.A.C. 5:37-5.7; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Mayor and/or Business Administrator be and are hereby authorized to execute the Service Agreement between the Township of West Orange and MLR/MetLife and to submit all necessary documents to the Director of the Division of Local Government Services within the State of New Jersey, Department of Community Affairs for appropriate review and approval. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Patricia Spango, Council President Adopted: August 30, 2011

("ASI") to perform the revaluation services as approved by Township Resolution No. 66-10 adopted March 9, 2010 in the total amount not to exceed $1,143,400 ("ASI Contract") ; and WHEREAS, in completing the revaluation there became certain issues caused by a mathematical error by ASI; and WHEREAS, the State of New Jersey and County Board of Taxation permitted an over ride to correct the error; and WHEREAS, the Township has met with ASI's representatives; and WHEREAS, the Township previously retained George F. Librizzi, CTA, IFAS, SCGREA as a consultant to assist with regard to the competitive contracting process to select the revaluation company; and WHEREAS, in light of the corrections needed, ASI has agreed to perform certain additional services at no cost including added assessments for 2011-12 and a Compliance Plan (known as Chapter 251, previously Chapter 101) conducted in 2011 for the year 2012 are specified by letter dated August 16, 2011 at no additional cost or expense to the Township (“Additional ASI Services”) ; and NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by Township Council of the Township of West Orange that ASI shall perform certain additional services for 2011 Added Assessments and 2011 Compliance Plan Ch. 251 for 2012 tax year; and it is further RESOLVED, that ASI has agreed to reduce the amount of ASI Contract by $5,000; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Township has determined to retain George F. Librizzi, CTA, IFAS, SCGREA as a consultant to monitor the compliance plan, supervise the added assessments,

2 and insure that all line items are entered in accordance with applicable law as defined herein as Additional ASI Services at no cost or expense to the Township ; and it is further RESOLVED, the retention of George F. Librizzi, CTA, IFAS, SCGREA at an expense of $5,000 is hereby approved as a non- fair and open process ; and it is further RESOLVED, that notice of this award shall be published in accordance with applicable law. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Patricia Spango, Council President Adopted: August 30 , 2011 THE FORM AND CONTENT OF THIS RESOLUTION IS HEREBY APPROVED BY: APPRAISAL SYSTEMS, INC. 196-11 8/30/2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, Public Service Electric & Gas Company (“ PSE&G), has submitted a Petition with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (“BPU”) for a determination under N.J.S.A. 40:55D- 19, that the proposed 230 kV North Central Reliability Project (“the Project”) is reasonably necessary for the service, convenience or welfare of the public; and WHEREAS, such Petition remains pending before the BPU; and WHEREAS , the Project will span fifteen municipalities within the State of New Jersey, including the Township of West Orange; and WHEREAS , PSE&G has proposed a Settlement Agreement to resolve any and all issues between the parties in connection with the Petition for the Project, a copy of which Settlement Agreement (“the Agreement”) is annexed hereto; and WHEREAS , the Project includes the upgrading of the transmission lines from the West Orange substation on Prospect Avenue and Mt. Pleasant Avenue, to the substation on Laurel Avenue in Livingston, and to the Roseland substation in Roseland, N.J., increasing the service capacity/voltage for those municipalities; and WHEREAS , the Project includes two transmission lines in the Township, an average increase of 15' in the height of the transmission towers, replacement of the current lattice towers with monopoles pursuant to the modern practice, such poles being sturdier and less visible; and WHEREAS , the proposed Agreement in summary provides that the Township of West Orange, agrees not to oppose the application before the BPU, agrees to cooperate with PSE&G during construction, including closing roads when needed, coordinating with the Police Department regarding traffic control arrangements, etc., in exchange for payment in stages of the sum of $111,608 for equipment and costs associated with the mitigation of construction of the project, and the sum of $33,970 for the planting of trees and other vegetation species for purposes of mitigating visual impacts of the Project; and WHEREAS , the Township Council of the Township of West Orange has reviewed the proposed settlement agreement and determined that it is satisfactory and wishes to authorize the appropriate Township officials to execute the agreement; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT, AND IT IS HEREBY, RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, that the Mayor shall be and hereby is authorized to execute, and the Municipal Clerk to attest to his signature, the Settlement Agreement between Public Service Electric & Gas Company and the Township of

West Orange with respect to the proposed 230 kV North Central Reliability Project, the application for which is pending with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (“BPU”) for a determination under N.J.S.A. 40:55D-19, all as referred to in the foregoing recitals and attached hereto, a copy of the fully executed Agreement to be kept on file in the Municipa l Clerk’s Office. __________________________________ Patricia Spango, Council President __________________________________ Karen J. pages.text: 193- 11 July 26, 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of July 26 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. () 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) : Potential Litigation/Contract

Appraisal Systems, Inc. (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on July 26, 2011 . Motion: Joe Krakoviak Second: Susan McCartney Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Patricia Spango M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: July 26, 2011

documents.title: AUTHORIZING COMPETITIVE CONTRACTING PROCESS FOR PRIVATE COLLECTION OF MUNICIPAL COURT DEBT

pages.text: 188-11 July 26, 2011 R ESOLUTION AUTHORIZING COMPETITIVE CONTRACTING PROCESS FOR PRIVATE COLLECTION OF MUNICIPAL COURT DEBT WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange is seeking to secure a contract with a qualified private collection agency to achieve maximum recovery of debts owed to the Township for fines and penalties iss ued by the Township’s Municipal Court.; and WHEREAS, under the Local Public Contracts Law N.J.S.A. 40A:11-4.1 competitive contracting may be used by local contracting units in lieu of the standard public bidding process for procurement of specialized goods and services where the price exceeds the bid threshold; and WHEREAS , insofar as this specific service is not enumerated in the Statute, subsection (k) permits the Township to seek approval from the Director of the Division of Local Government Services. That permission was granted to the Township; and WHEREAS, the Township meets the criteria of Local Public Contracts Law N.J.S.A. 40a:11-4.1.3 which allows the use of a methodology to rank and evaluate proposals received . This method will secure the most advantageous agreement for the Township. NOW HEREBY BE IT RESOLVED , by the Council of the Township of West Orange, that Competitive Contract Process shall be i nitiated for the purpose of receiving proposal s for the Private Collection of Municipal Court Debt pursuant to the policies and procedures of the Administrative Office of the Courts (“AOC”). The competitive contracting process shall be administered by the Purchasing Agent, Business Administrator , Municipal Attorney, Municipal Court Administrator, and the Chief Financial Officer according to the local public contracts law. Any contracts awarded under this process shall be made by resolution of the governing body of the Township of West Orange. ________________________________ Patricia Spango, Council President Karen J. Carnevale, Township Clerk Adopted: July 26, 2011

(New Jersey Local Unit Pay-To-Play Laws), the Township must award by resolution all goods and services contracts with a dollar amount between $17,500 and $35,999. These contracts are not bid, but vendors are still responsible to provide political contribution and company disclosure information in order to do business with the Township. WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.4 et seq., when the cost of goods and/or services that fall between $17,500 and the bid threshold of $36,000 in the aggregate, an approval by resolution must be in place prior to contract; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange Engineering Department proposes to construct storm sewer improvements at the intersection of Woodland Avenue and Stevens Terrace; and WHEREAS, the West Orange Engineering Department retained the services of G. C. Stewart Associates of Essex Fells, New Jersey 07021 to prepare plans for the proposed drainage improvements; and WHEREAS, a request for quotes for the required work to be performed was requested from several contractors; and WHEREAS, the following quotes were submitted to this department: 1. Shauger Properties Services, Inc. $36,995.00 429 Dodd Street East Orange, New Jersey 07017 WHEREAS, Grabowski Construction, Inc. has performed work for the Township and is qualified to do this project; and WHEREAS, Grabowski Construction, Inc. completed and submitted a Business Entity Disclosure Certification which certifies the business entity has not made any reportable contributions to a political or candidate committee in the Township of West Orange in the previous one year, and that the contract will prohibit Grabowski Construction, Inc. from making any reportable contributions through the term of the contract. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Council of the Township of West Orange authorizes the Purchasing Agent on behalf of the Township to issue and execute a Purchase Order for the foregoing to Grabowski Construction, Inc. of 770 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, New Jersey 07052 in the amount of $32,457.00 with funds certified available by the Chief financial Officer; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Business Administrator is hereby authorized to arrange to pay for the foregoing in accordance with the terms of the purchase order. 180-11 July 26, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, electronic ticketing for traffic and other violations can increase the accuracy of summonses issued and reduce the time required to issue summonses; and WHEREAS, the Township desires to have certain technology in its police cars including cameras/microphones which are used when motor vehicle stops occur and computers which can permit officers to enter motor vehicle checks and motor vehicle accident reports on a real time basis and keep the officers from having to go into headquarters to prepare and finalize these reports; and WHEREAS, the Township desires to implement e-ticketing in a manner which interfaces seamlessly with the New Jersey Administrative Office of the Court s ; and WHEREAS, pursuant to the Local Public Contracts Law N.J.S.A. 40A:11-12 municipalities are permitted to use the state contract without public bidding; and WHEREAS, Gold Type Business Machines, Inc. ("GTBM") of Rutherford, New Jersey is in possession of State Contract No. 75583 for e-ticketing products and services including the installation and financing of certain hardware including cameras, microphones, license plate readers and the server; and WHEREAS, GTBM's e-ticketing products and services interface seamlessly with the New Jersey Administrative Office of the Courts which will lessen the personnel needed to input the tickets at the Municipal Court; and WHEREAS, the Township's Purchasing Agent has certified that she considers the proposal to be fair and reasonable; and WHEREAS, e-ticketing will be funded via a per ticket fee paid quarterly with no upfront capital expenditures; and WHEREAS, this award of contract is contingent upon sufficient funds being appropriated in the Township's budgets as certified to by the Chief Financial Officer; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE

Adopted: July 26, 2011 175-11 AGREEMENT THIS AGREEMENT, made this day of July 20 11 by and between: TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, a municipal corporation of the State of New Jersey, having its principal offices at 66 Main Street, West Orange, New Jersey, hereinafter referred to as "Township"; and POLICE ATHLETIC LEAGUE, a nonprofit corporation of the State of New Jersey having its principal offices at Prospect Place, West Orange, New Jersey, hereinafter referred to as " PAL ". W I T N E S S E T H: WHEREAS, the Township desires to provide certain recreational services, social services, activities, and facilities to the residents of the Township of West Orange; and WHEREAS, it is the purpose of this agreement to recite the terms and conditions under which the foregoing shall be provided; and NOW THEREFORE , in consideration of the foregoing and of the mutual covenants hereinafter stated, the parties do hereby agree as follows: 1. F or the period of January 1, 2011 to

December 31, 2011 PAL shall provide and make available to West Orange residents, services and facilities for participation by such residents of West Orange. 2. The foregoing facilities and services shall be supervised and operated by personnel provided by PAL , wh ose personnel shall be solely the employees of the volunteers of PAL who is responsible to pay them , where appropriate, at the sole discretion of PAL . 3. PAL shall provide, at PAL expense, Workers Compensation Insurance, covering its employees performing hereunder, and public liability insurance with limits of Five Hundred Thousand ($500,000.00) Dollars to One Million ($1,000,000.00) Dollars for the areas and locations where the recreational facilities are conducted. Said insurance shall cover the interest of the Township and shall be with carriers satisfactory to the Township and authorized to do business in New Jersey. Certificates evidencing the foregoing shall be furnished to the Township upon execution of this Agreement. 4. PAL agrees to indemnify the Township and save it harmless, including Township's employees, agents and servants, from and against any and all losses, claims, liabilities and expenses which may arise or be claimed against the Township, its agents, servants or employees in connection with any phase of this Agreement. 5. Neither this Agreement nor the monies to grow

hereunder may be assigned. 6 . PAL acknowledges that it has read N.J.S.A. 10:2-1, et seq., of the Revised Statutes of the State of New Jersey (Discrimination in Employment on Public Works, Contract Provisions), the terms of which are incorporated herein as though expressly set forth at length. PAL agrees to comply with and be bound by the provisions thereof. 7. It is understood that this Agreement shall be deemed effective as of January 1,2011 . 8. Township shall pay to PAL for the services to be provided hereunder for the full one-year term, the sum of Twelve Thousand ($ 12 , 0 00.00) Dollars. 9. The manner of payment shall be as determined jointly by the President of PAL and Director of the Department of Recreation of Township. 10. The parties hereto agree that the provisions of the “New Jersey Prevailing Wage Act” shall apply hereto the extent held applicable to a volunteer organization. Accordingly, PAL agrees to comply with the provisions of N.J.S.A. 34:11-56.25 through 34:11-56.33, the provisions of which are hereby in corporated by reference as though stated at length herein. PAL hereby declares that it is aware of the prevailing wage rates on file in the Township Hall of Township pursuant to said Act and agrees to comply therewith to the extent held applicable to volunteer organizations. PAL further agrees as follows:

A. All covered employees of PAL performing services hereunder shall be paid not less than the prevailing wage rate as specified. B . PAL shall maintain accurate records, showing name, kind of work performed and actual hourly rate of wages paid to each employee employed hereunder. Such records shall be maintained for three (3) years from date of payment and shall be available for inspection by the Township's Business Administrator or his designee on request. C. PAL shall post the prevailing wage rate for each employee performing worker hereunder, as determined by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry of the State of New Jersey, including the effective date of any changes thereof, in a prominent and easily accessible place and the principal Office of PAL. D. If it is found that any employee of PAL is paid less than the required wage rates Township may, on written notice to PAL, terminate PAL's rights to proceed hereunder, or as to such portion of services rendered hereunder as to which there has been a failure to pay the required wages. Township may then arrange to prosecute the rendering of the services hereunder by other means, in which even PAL shall be liable to Township for all costs and damages incurred by Township. E. It is specifically understood that the provisions of this paragraph shall not apply to such persons engaged by

PAL render services hereunder who are performing such services as volunteers without remuneration. F. PAL agrees to be bound by the provisions of Schedule A attached hereto and made a part hereof. I N WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused these presents to be signed by their proper corporate officers and their property corporate seals to be hereto affixed the day and year first above written. 175-11 " SCHEDULE A " (I) During the performance of this contract the contractor agrees as follows: a. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable, will not discriminate against any employee of applicant for employment because of age, race, creed, color, national, origin, ancestry, marital status or sex. The contractor will take affirmative action to ensure that such applicants are recruited and employed, and that employees are treated during employment, without regard to their age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status or sex. Such action shall include, but not be limited to the following: employment, upgrading, demotion, or transfer; recruitment or recruitment advertising; layoff or termination; rates of pay or other forms of compensation; and selection for training, including apprenticeship. The contractor agrees to post in conspicuous places, available to employees and applicants for employment, notices to be provided by the Public Agency Compliance Officer setting forth provisions of this non- discrimination clause; b. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable

will, in all solicitations or advertisements for employees placed by or on behalf of the contractor, state that all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, martial status or sex; c. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable, will send to each labor union or representative or workers with which it has a collective bargaining agreement or other contract or understanding, a notice, to be provided by the agency contracting officer advising the labor union or worker's representative of the contractor's commitments under this act and shall post copies of the notice in conspicuous places available to employees and applicants for employment. d. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable, agrees to comply with any regulations promulgated by the Treasure pursuant to P.L. 1975,c.127, as amended and supplemented from time to time. (II) The contractor or subcontractor agrees to attempt in good faith to employ minority and female workers consistent with the applicable county employment goals prescribed by section 5.2 of the Regulations promulgated by the Treasurer pursuant to P.L. 1975, c.127, as amended and supplemented from time to time or in accordance with a binding determination of the applicable county employment goals

determined by the Affirmative Action Office pursuant to section 5.2 of the Regulations promulgated by the Treasurer pursuant to P.L. 1975, c. 127, as amended and supplemented from time to time. (III) The contractor or subcontractor agrees to inform in writing appropriate recruitment agencies in the area, including employment agencies, placements bureaus, colleges, universities, labor unions, that it does not discriminate on the basis of age, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status or sex, and that it will discontinue the use of any recruitment agency which engages in direct or indirect or indirect discriminatory practices. (IV) The Contractor or subcontractor agrees to revise any of its testing procedure, if necessary, to assure that all personnel testing conforms with the principles of job- related testing, as established by the statutes and court decisions of the State of New Jersey and as established by applicable federal law and applicable federal court decisions. (V) The contractor or subcontractor agrees to review all procedures relating to transfer, upgrading, downgrading and layoff to ensure that all such actions are taken without regard to age, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status or sex, and conform with the applicable
employment goals, consistent with the statutes and court decisions of the State of New Jersey, and applicable federal Law and applicable federal court decisions.

1 152-11 July 26 , 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , on May 17, 2011, the Township Council of the Township of West Orange (the “Township Council”) adopted Resolution No. 115-11 ; and WHEREAS , Resolution No. 115-11 approved a proposed settlement of claims related to alleged violations of the Uniform Fire Code (the “Violations”) by Telgian Corporation (“Telgian”) and/or Sears Holdings Corporation (“Sears”) , which were brought after a fire occurred within the Dollar Tree Store at West Orange Plaza, 235 Prospect Avenue, West Orange, New Jersey, 07052 (the “Property”); and WHEREAS , Resolution No. 115-11 authorized the Township to release and settle any and all claims relating to the Violations for the amount of $75,000; and WHEREAS , the proposed release and settlement agreement for the amount of $75,000 has not been formally executed by the Township, Sears and/or Telgian; and WHEREAS , attorneys for the Township, Telgian and Sears subsequently engaged in additional discussions regarding the Township’s ability to further prosecute the Violations against the landlord and/or owner of the P roperty ; and WHEREAS , Summons No. 031628 was issued against the owner and/or landlord of the Property, Kruvant Associates and/or West Orange Plaza, LLC (the “Owner”) , seeking to enforce the Violations against those entities in the Township’s Municipal Court ; and WHEREAS , after Resolution No. 115-11 was approved, Sears and/or Telgian increased its offer to resolve the Violations to $77,500, in order to settle globally all outstanding issues with respect to the Violations, including but not limited to the Township’s prosecution of the Violations against the Owner; and WHEREAS , Telgian and Sears have executed the revised settlement agreement, which supersedes the prior agreement, a copy of which is annexed hereto as Exhibit “A” ; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by the Township Council, that the revised settlement agreement between the Township, Sears and Telgian, annexed hereto as Exhibit “A , ” is hereby approved; THEREFORE, BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Mayor is hereby authorized to execute the agreement annexed hereto; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that, for the reasons stated herein, this Resolution shall supersede and void Resolution No. 115-11; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED , that a true copy of the Agreement shall remain on file with the Township Clerk for inspection by the public. Patricia Spango, Council President K aren J. Carnevale , Municipal Clerk Adopted: Ju ly 2 6 , 2011

pages.text: 1 64 -11 June 28 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of June 28 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President June 28, 2011

151-11 June 28, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , the Township has performed a revaluation of all properties located in the Township pursuant to Title 54 of the New Jersey Statutes Annotated; and WHEREAS , under the terms of the revaluation contract, the revaluation vendor, Appraisal System Inc. ("ASI") is obligated to defend all valuations for two (2) ; and WHEREAS , approximately 877 tax appeals were timely filed with the vast bulk pending before the County Board of Taxation ; and WHEREAS , ASI and the Tax Assessor will attend and assist with regard to the review and prosecution of these matters; and WHEREAS , the Township must retain legal counsel to assist it with regard to the various tax appeals; and WHEREAS , the Law Department has reviewed various proposals and recommends the engagement of Stephen E. Schwartz, Esq. to assist with regard to these hearings which will be scheduled for several months with approximately thirty (30) cases being handled each session; and WHEREAS , the Law Department has negotiated a flat rate of $350 per session with Mr. Schwartz inclusive of all preparation, prosecution, follow up and related services regardless of how many hours each session lasts inclusive of travel, parking and other expenses ; and WHEREAS , the retention of tax appeal counsel was handled through a fair and open process of in accordance with applicable law; and WHEREAS , the Township currently estimates approximately thirty (30) sessions which will cause a total expenditure of approximately $ 10,500 ; and WHEREAS , the current budget has allocated sufficient funds for this expenditure and the Chief Financial Officer has certified the availability of funds; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by Township Council of the Township of West Orange that the Township be and is hereby authorized to retain Stephen E. Schwartz, Esq. as special tax counsel at a rate of $350 per session before the County Board of Taxation up to a maximum expenditure of $10,500; and it is further RESOLVED , that a copy of this Resolution shall be published and available in accordance with applicable law. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: June 28, 2011

Township of West Orange County of Essex Audit Report Year 2010 COMMENTS AND RECOMMENDATIONS December 31, 2010 FINDINGS-Capital Fund 1 1- FINDING: Green Acre matching grant receivable on Ordinance # 1992-04 of $103,270.02 has been carried for a number of years. 2- RECOMMENDATION: The receivable should be reviewed in order to determine it collectability. 3- CORRECTIVE ACTION: The Township Engineer has resolved all outstanding issues with the Essex County Engineer, but still must satisfy the concerns of the County Counsel. 4- IMPLEMENTATION DATE: Fall 2011 1- FINDING: There is a receivable associated with the 2005 NJDEA loan. The loan is amortized with interest, yet the receivable has not changed. 2- RECOMMENDATION: The receivable of $2,447,091 should be reviewed in order to determine its collectability. 3- CORRECTIVE ACTION: The contract for the Mayfair Sanitary Sewer Improvements was awarded on November 4, 2010, and subsequently approved by the NJ Department of Environmental Protection and the NJ Environmental Trust, and construction will commence shortly. 4- IMPLEMETATION DATE: Fall 2011 FINDINGS-Dedication by Rider 2 1- FINDING: Certain Accounts classified herein as Special Deposits in the General Trust Fund may be subject to the provision of Dedication by Rider, N.J.S. 40A:4-29. Statutory regulations require that resolutions be adopted by the Governing Body and Subsequent approval by the Division of Local Government Services for any account dedicated by rider to the municipal budget 2- RECOMMENDATION: That certain trust accounts be reviewed by Township officials for possible inclusion in the municipal budget under the provisions if dedication by Rider, N.J.S. 40A-39. 3- CORRECTIVE ACTION: All Trust Accounts are being reviewed, and continue to be reviewed to ascertain, if a Dedication by Rider is necessary. 4- IMPLEMENTATION DATE: July 1, 2011 FINDINGS-Police Special Duty 3 1- FINDING: A review of activity for police special duty work disclosed that fees are not being collected from vendors before the work is scheduled as required. This has resulted in the

Township financing the cost for police special duty work. 2- RECOMMENDATION: That vendors pay in advance for projects in which police officers are scheduled to provide police special duty. 3- CORRECTIVE ACTION: The Township Attorney’s Office is in the process of preparing a Sample Agreement, in conjunction with Police Administration, to be used on all special duty assignments that call for an escrow account being established. 4- IMPLEMENTATION DATE: October 1, 2011 (already partially implemented) FINDINGS-Revenue Department 4 1- FINDING: The rental fee being charged for uses of a second room at the Toby Katz Community Center was not in agreement with the approved fee schedule. 2- RECOMMENDATION: That the fee charged for rental of a second room at the Toby Katz Community Center agrees with the fee schedule. 3- CORRECTIVE ACTION: In the spring of 2010, the operation of the Toby Katz Community Center was moved from the Katz Center to the Main Office of the Recreation Department. Responsibility for the facility was shifted from a part time employee to a full time member of the office staff. 4- IMPLEMENTATION DATE: Already Implemented 1- FINDING: not all program applications requested were made available for audit. 2- RECOMMENDATION: All program applications be made available for audit. 3- CORRECTIVE ACTION: One Team Registration from an area high school for the 2010 High School Summer Basketball was missing and presumed to have been properly submitted. The problem was explained to the Program Coordinator, a part time employee. The team was placed on probation for the summer of 2011. 4- IMPLEMENTATION DATE: Already implemented

pages.text: 146-11 June 28, 2011 RESOLUTION REQUESTING APPROVAL OF ITEMS OF REVENUE AND APPROPRIATION NJS 40A:4-87 WHEREAS, NJS 40A:4-87 provides that the Director of the Division of Local Government Services may approve the insertion of any special item of revenue in the budget of any county or municipality when such item shall have been made available by law and the amount was not determined at the time of the adoption of the budget; and WHEREAS , the Director may also approve the insertion of an item of appropriation for equal amount , NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange in the County of Essex, in the State of New Jersey, hereby requests the Director of the Division of Local Government Services to approve the insertion of an item of revenu e in the budget of the year 20 1 1 in the sum of $ 12,712 , which is now available from NJ D epartment of Law and Public Safety - Cops in Shops Program , i n the amount of $ 12,712 . BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the like sum of $ 12,712 . is hereby appropriated under the caption NJ Department of Law and Public Safety-Cops in Shops Program. and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the abo ve is the result of funds from NJ D epartment of H ighway Traffic Safety- Cops in Shops Program , in the amount of $ 12,712 . pages.text: 145 -11 June 14 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of June 14 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. () 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

Litigation City of Orange Tax Appeal Holland v. Township of West Orange (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on June 14 , 2011. Motion: Patty Spango Second: Victor Cirilo Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011

140-11 June 14, 2011 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange awarded a contract to Shauger Property Services, Inc., having its principal place of business at 429 Dodd Street, East Orange, New Jersey 07017 for West Orange High School Bleacher and Storage Installation at the football field, 51 Conforti Avenue, West Orange, New Jersey 07052; and WHEREAS, the Township Council by Resolution No. 76-10 dated March 23, 2010 awarded a contract for a lump sum bid of $1,083,379.71, which sum includes alternate bids 1, 2 & 3; and WHEREAS, alternate bid No. 1 in the amount of $111,396.89 for the installation of an all weather track system BSS-200 surface at the existing “D” Zone on field was previously approved; and WHEREAS, Change Order No. 1 dated June 29, 2010 in the amount of $21,441.00 was previously approved; and WHEREAS, Change Order No. 2 dated October 5, 2010 in the amount of $19,770.91 for Change Order Proposals No. 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 & 11 is hereby added to the contract sum of $1,083,379.71 and Change Order No. 1 in the amount of $21,441.00 increasing total construction costs to $1,124,591.62; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer and the West Orange Board of Education recommend that this Change Order as being necessary and beneficial; and WHEREAS, sufficient funds are available; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing; and NOW THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED , by the Township Council of West Orange that Change Order No. 2 with Shauger Property Services, Inc., in the amount of $19,770.91 for the Change Order Proposals at the West Orange High School Football Field are hereby approved and the Township Council further authorizes the Mayor to execute Change Order No. 2 dated October 5, 2010. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011

139-11 June 14, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , on February 17, 2011 the Township of West Orange advertised for bids for the project entitled “2010 Roadway Improvements- Phase I- Various Streets”, prepared by the Engineering Division for the Township; and WHEREAS, the Township on March 15, 2011 received 19 bids for this project; and WHEREAS, on March 29, 2011 the Township Council by Resolution No. 63-11 awarded a contract for this project to the lowest respon sive bidder, A & J Contractor’s Group, 105 Federal Road, Monroe Township, New Jersey in the amount of $512,777.30; and WHEREAS , the bid and contract were based on unit prices; and WHEREAS , the street s included in this project included Central Place, Glebe Street, Cary Street, Lafayette Street , portions of Chestnut Street and Cherry Street and all of Franklin Avenue; and WHEREAS , A & J Contractor’s Group, Inc. proceeded with the improvements associated with th is project; and WHEREAS , as the work neared completion the Engineering Division determined it significantly underestimated the quantities of work on a portion of Franklin Avenue between Chestnut Street and the Montclair line; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated June 1, 2011 restated the estimated quantities of six major items of construction omitted from the original bid quantity estimate; and WHEREAS , those additional bid quantities as well as a supplemental item for culvert repair on Central Place are stated in Change Order No. 1 dated June 1, 2011 for this project; and WHEREAS , the restated quantities for the six major items along with the supplemental items result in an additional estimated cost for $90,000.00; and WHEREAS , the Township Engineer by letter dated June 1, 2011 recommends Change Order No. 1 for this project be approved to reflect the estimated costs for the project as described which included Franklin Avenue from Main Street to the Montclair line ; and WHEREAS , the Township Council concurs the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that Change Order No. 1 in the amount of $90,000.00 for the project 2010 Roadway Improvements- Phase 1, Various Streets with A & J Contractor’s Group, Monroe Township, New Jersey

be approved. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Township Council approves this Change Order based on the statements and representations of the Township Engineer that quantities for several major items of work on Franklin Avenue and in particular the section of Franklin Avenue between Chestnut and the Montclair line were significantly underestimated and that this Change Order with the restated quantities enables the Township and its contractor to complete the project and in particular Franklin Avenue as described in the bid documents. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011
