pages.text: 138-11 June 14, 2011 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING A “WINDOW” CONTRACT FOR STORM SEWER AND BUILDING RENOVATION 230 & 232 EAGLE ROCK AVE N UE Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.4 et seq. (New Jersey Local Unit Pay-To-Play Laws), the Township must award by resolution all goods and services contracts with a dollar amount between $17,500.00 and $35,999.00. These contracts are not bid, but vendors are still responsible to provide political contribution and company disclosure information in order to do business with the Township. WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.4 et seq., when the cost of goods and/or services that fall between $17,500.00 and the bid threshold of $36,000.00 in the aggregate, an approval by resolution must be in place prior to contract; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange Engineering Department proposes to relocate and reroute an existing 30 inch storm sewer on properties 230 and 232 Eagle Rock Avenue; and WHERAS, the required easement for the rerouted storm sewer was acquired from the owners of 230 and 232 Eagle Rock Avenue; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange also propose s to renovate and restore an existing residential structure, namely 230 Eagle Rock Avenue, under which the existing 30 inch storm sewer is presently located; and WHEREAS, the existing storm sewer has deteriorated and caused structural damage to a portion of the existing residential structure, specifically the one-car garage area; and WHEREAS, the West Orange Engineering Department retained the services of G. C. Stewart Associates, Inc. of Essex Fells, New Jersey 07021 to prepare site plans for the proposed drainage re-alignment in addition to the related site work; and WHEREAS, Gerhard Huegel, Senior Architect with the West Orange Engineering Department prepared plans for the renovation and restoration of the residential structure; and WHEREAS, a request for quotes for the required work to be performed was requested from several construction contractors; and WHEREAS, the following quotes were submitted to this department: 1. Helios Construction, Inc. $32,630.00 1321A Allenhurst Avenue Ocean, New Jersey 07712 2. Shauger Properties Services, Inc. $41,411.00 429 Dodd Street East Orange, New Jersey 07017 3. S. Lemo Construction LLC $47,300.00 18 East Harvest Avenue

East Hanover, New Jersey 07936 4. Grabowski Construction, Inc. $51,090.00 770 Northfield Avenue West Orange, New Jersey 07052 WHEREAS, Helios Construction, Inc. has performed work for the Township and is qualified to do this project; and WHEREAS, Helios Construction, Inc. completed and submitted a Business Entity Disclosure Certification which certifies the business entity has not made any reportable contributions to a political or candidate committee in the Township of West Orange in the previous one year, and that the contract will prohibit Helios Construction, Inc. from making any reportable contributions through the term of the contract. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Council of the Township of West Orange authorizes the Purchasing Agent on behalf of the Township to issue and execute a Purchase Order for the foregoing to Helios Construction, Inc. of 1321 Allenhurst Avenue, Ocean, New Jersey 07712 in the amount of $32,630.00 with funds certified available by the Chief financial Officer; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Business Administrator is hereby authorized to arrange to pay for the foregoing in accordance with the terms of the purchase order. BE IT FURTHER that the Business Disclosure Entity Certification and the Determination of Value be placed on file with this resolution and notice of this award will be published in accordance with the applicable law. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011

135-11 June 14, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , the Township requires the services of labor counsel with regard to various matters including collective bargaining agreements, disciplinary issues, and related matters; and WHEREAS , the Township engaged in a fair and open process pursuant to N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.4 et seq. ; and WHEREAS , by Resolution No. 51-11 adopted March 8, 2011, the Township Council approved the retention of certain counsel including Scarinci Hollenbeck of Lyndhurst, New Jersey; and WHEREAS , the Township's budget issues have necessitated greater negotiations and involvement by labor counsel; and WHEREAS , on April 12, 2011, the Council adopted Resolution No. 82-11 authorizing $15,000 in legal fees and expenses during 2011 for Scarinci Hollenbeck concerning labor and employment matters ; and WHEREAS, two unfair labor charges have been filed with the Department of Labor and referred to the Office of Administrative Law concerning certain layoffs which require representation; and WHEREAS , the Township Attorney recommends adoption of a resolution authorizing the Township to increase the allocation for Scarinci Hollenbeck with regard to labor services; and WHEREAS , the Chief Financial Officer of the Township of West Orange has certified the availability of funds in accordance with the "cap" set forth herein; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by Township Council of the Township of West Orange that the Mayor be and is hereby authorized to execute the annexed agreement to provide legal services between the Township of West Orange and Scarinci Hollenbeck; and it is further RESOLVED , that the "cap" of $15,000 is hereby extended to $30,000 for fees and expenses with regard to the services provided herein; and it is further RESOLVED , that the Municipal Clerk of the Township of West Orange shall cause notice of this award to be published in accordance with applicable law and available for inspection during normal business hours in the office of the Municipal Clerk of the Township of West Orange. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011

Ed/resolution/ 2010estimatedtaxresolution 133-11 June 14, 2011 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE TAX COLLECTOR TO PREPARE AND MAIL ESTIMATED TAX BILLS IN ACCORDANCE WITH P.L. 1994, c. 72 WHEREAS, the Essex County Board of Freeholders and the Township of West Orange have not adopted the Essex County Budget and the Township of West Orange Budget for 2011 and the West Orange Township Tax Collector will be unable to mail the Township’s 20 1 1 tax bills on a timely basis; WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange Tax Collector in consultation with the West Orange Township Chief Financial Officer has computed an estimated tax levy in accordance with N.J.S.A. 54:4-66.3, and they have both signed a certification showing the tax levies for the previous year, the tax rates and the range of permitted estimated tax levies; WHEREAS, in accordance with Chapter 72, P.L. 1994, the Township Council requests the Director of the Division of Local Government Services to approve the estimated tax levy exceeding 105% listed below. Approval will enable the Township to meet its financial obligations, maintain the tax collection rate, provide uniformity for tax payments and save the unnecessary cost of interest expenses on borrowing. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, IN THE COUNTY OF ESSEX AND STATE OF NEW JERSEY on this 1 4 th day of June , 20 1 1 , as follows: 1. The Township of West Orange Tax Collector is hereby authorized and directed to prepare and issue estimated tax bills for the Township for the third installment of 2011 taxes. The Tax Collector shall proceed upon approval from the Director and take such actions as are permitted and required by L. 1994, c.72 (N.J.S.A. 54:4-66.2 and 54.4-66.3) 2. The entire estimated tax levy for 2011 is hereby set at $ 199,342,478.08 In accordance with law the third installment of 20 1 1 taxes shall not be subject to interest until the later of August 10 or the twenty fifth calendar day after the date the estimated tax bills were mailed. The estimated tax bills shall contain a notice specifying the date on which interest may begin to accrue. CERTIFICATION I, Karen J. Carnevale , Municipal Clerk of the Township of West Orange in the County of Essex, do hereby certify that the foregoing is a true and correct copy of a resolution duly adopted by the Township Council at a regular meeting held on the 1 4 th day of June , 20 1 1. IN WITNESS WHEREOF I have hereunto set my hand and affixed the seal of said Township the 1 4 th day of June , 201 1 . _____________________________ _____________________________ Karen J. Carnevale S al M. Anderton Municipal Clerk Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011

132-11 June 14, 2011 TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE COUNTY OF ESSEX, NEW JERSEY AUTHORIZATION FOR SALE OF NOTES FOR SPECIAL EMERGENCY APPROPRIATION SEVERANCE LIABILTIES RESULTING FROM ACCRUED LEAVE IN CONNECTION WITH THE RETIRMENT OF EMPLOYEES WHEREAS, an ordinance (Ordinance No. 2322-11) has been adopted creating a special emergency appropriation of $ 448,900 to meet certain expenses to be incurred for severance liabilities resulting from accrued leave in connection with the retirement of employees and N.J.S.A.40A:4-53 provides for the creation of a special emergency appropriation for the purpose above mentioned; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, COUNTY OF ESSEX, NEW JERSEY (not less than two-thirds of all the members, thereof, affirmatively concurring) that in accordance with N.J.S.A:40A- 55: 1. The sum of $ 448,900 is hereby appropriated for severance liabilities resulting from accrued leave in connection with the retirement of employees, and shall be deemed a special emergency appropriation as defined and provided for in N.J.S.A.40A:4-53. 2. That an emergency note or notes be authorized not in excess of $ 448,900, the amount appropriated by the Ordinance stated above. 3. That said note or notes shall be issued in fiscal 2011 and may be renewed from time to time and at least 1/5 of all such notes and renewals, thereof, shall mature and be paid in each fiscal year thereafter until all are paid. _____________________________ Sal M. Anderton, Council President I hereby certify that the above Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a meeting held on June 14, 2011 . _____________________________ Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk

Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton , Council President Adopted: June 14, 2011

pages.text: 128-11 May 31, 2011 RESO L UTION 2011 Contract for the Food & Beverage Concession Stand at the Ginny Duenkel Municipal Pool WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange has a Food & Beverage Concession Stand located at the Ginny Duenkel Municipal Pool which has been made available for a private business to rent and operate during the summer season; and WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange did advertise and receive bids for the Pool Concession Stand in 2009 and Bagelwich Bagel Bakery, 658 Bloomfield Avenue, Verona, New Jersey as the most responsible and responsive bidder; and WHEREAS , the Bagelwich Bagel Bakery has satisfactorily performed their services and complied with financial agreements during the last two summer seasons; and WHEREAS, contracted prices for menu items and rental fees have not no changed; and WHEREAS , the Township will renew the contract for the 2011 summer season pursuant with the Local Public Contract s Law 40A:11-15(10) which states the providing of food services for any term can not exce ed three years. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Municipal Council of the Township of West Orange that the 2011 seasonal contract for the operation of the Food & Concession Stand at the Ginny Duenkel Pool located in the Township of West Orange shall remain with: Bagelwich Bagel Bakery to pay the Township $8,751.51. BE IT FUR THER RESOLVED that payments will be received by the Chief Financial Officer in accordance to the bid specifications. ___________________________ ________________________ _____ _ Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: May 31, 2011

127-11 May 31, 2011 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the Open Space and Recreation Committee at its meeting of May 9, 2011 voted to recommend to the Township Council the acquisition of two parcels of undeveloped land on Wiley Terrace known as Block 159.08, Lots 53 and 55; and WHEREAS, these two parcels are adjacent to a parcel of undeveloped Township owned land located behind Fire Station No. 3 which is located on Ridgeway Avenue at Wiley Terrace; and WHEREAS, the acquisition will be partially funded using a Planning Incentive Grant from the Green Acres Program; and WHEREAS, this Grant requires the Township to obtain property appraisals, land surveys, environmental assessments and title insurance; and WHEREAS, the Grant will fund a portion of these professional services if the property is acquired; and WHEREAS, the Township Administration desires to pursue the acquisition of these two parcels as recommended by the Township’s Open Space and Recreation Committee; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs with the recommendation of the Open Space and Recreation Committee. NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of Township of West Orange that the Township’s Administration is authorized to proceed with the acquisition of Block 159.08, Lots 53 and 55 on Wiley Terrace for open space and recreation purposes as recommended by the Township’s Open Space and Recreation Committee. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Township Administration is authorized to solicit proposals for professional services associated with these acquisitions for property appraisals, land surveys and environmental assessments. Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: May 31, 2011 Approved as to form on the basis of the facts provided:

125-11 May 31, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, on June 15, 1972, the West Orange Senior Citizens Housing Association, a non- profit corporation of the State of New Jersey ("Sponsor) and the Township of West Orange, a municipal corporation in the County of Essex and State of New Jersey (the "Township") entered into a Tax Abatement Agreement ("Tax Agreement") which was duly authorized and agreed to, and WHEREAS, the Tax Agreement provided that certain payments in lieu of taxes ("PILOT") were to be paid by the Sponsor based upon a formula that did not include any rental subsidies received in accordance with the regulations and formulas promulgated by the Department of Housing and Urban Development ("HUD"); and WHEREAS, Sponsor recently realized that it has been paying the Township PILOT amounts that include d rental subsidies received through HUD; and WHEREAS, Sponsor has requested that these payments including the rental subsidies totaling $134,840, as of June 30, 2010, ("Over Payments") be returned by the Township as they were paid in error; and WHEREAS, the Sponsor and the Township have met on several occasions to discuss this issue; and WHEREAS, the parties have agreed to resolve this matter amicably without the need for additional professional fees and delay ; and WHEREAS , annexed hereto is a copy of the Settlement Agreement, which provides as follows: 1. The PILOT due and owing to the Township from the Sponsor shall be reduced to $60,000 per year until the Sponsor receives full credit for the Over Payments made to the Township. 2. Once the Over Payments are credited to the Sponsor, Sponsor shall resume paying the Township its full PILOT as calculated pursuant to the provisions of the Tax Agreement. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, that the Mayor be and is hereby authorized to execute the annexed Settlement Agreement between the Township of West Orange and West Orange Senior Citizens Housing Association ; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Municipal Clerk be and is hereby authorized to attest to the Mayor’s signature on the Settlement Agreement . Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: May 31, 2011

124-11 May 31, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township awarded a certain project entitled Construction of an Entrance Canopy Enclosure Addition to West Orange Police Facility (the "Project") to Automatic Door Systems, LLC of North Arlington, New Jersey ("ADS") dated May 26, 2010 in the amount of $104,850 plus $10,000 for alternate number 1 for a total of $1 1 4,850 (the "Contract Amount"); and WHEREAS, by contract dated October 6, 2008, the Township entered into an agreement with Herbst-Musciano Architects/Planners of Cedar Knolls, New Jersey ("Herbst-Musciano") to perform certain construction contract administration services; and WHEREAS, the Project's start date and progress has been delayed as a result of ADS personnel issues, fire suppression analysis issues, and weather/winter issues; and WHEREAS , the Project's delays have increased the cost and need for architectural services; and WHEREAS, the initial contract with Herbst-Musciano provided for a fee of $8,000 for construction contract administration services not to exceed six (6) months which timeframe has expired; and WHEREAS , on May 3, 2011, a Resolution was adopted by the Township Council approving a Change Order No. 1 for electrical additions in an amount not to exceed $5,000 or an increase of 4.4 percent of the original contract amount of $114,850, bringing the total contract sum to a maximum of $119,850 ; and WHEREAS, on May 23, 2011 a meeting was conducted with representatives of ADS and Herbst -Musciano wherein it was agreed that a change order will occur whereby the ADS contract will be reduced by $7,500 and such monies will be paid to Herbst-Musciano for completion off all construction contract administrative services; and WHEREAS, the result of this Change Order will be no net economic impact on the Township and will facilitate the contract being completed at the earliest possible date; and WHEREAS, the Legal Department recommends approval of this Change Order; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, that Change Order No. 3 be and is hereby approved whereby the Automatic Door Systems, LLC contract will be reduced by $7,500 to $112,350 and the Herbst-Musciano contract will be increased by $7,500; and it is further RESOLVED that notice of this resolution shall be published in accordance with applicable law. Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: May 31, 2011

120-11 May 31, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , PARNELL BEAUBRUN, is the owner of the real property and dwelling house at 41 Sunnyside Road (Block 175.23, Lot 21); and WHEREAS , the property owner timely appealed his 2009 assessment for real property taxes to the Essex County Board of Taxation; and WHEREAS , at the time of the 2009 appeal the subject property was assessed as follows: LAND: $20,000.00 BLDG.: $66,700.00 $86,700.00 and WHEREAS , when the aforesaid appeal was filed the property owner had not paid his 2009 taxes and was thus delinquent; and WHEREAS , as a delinquent taxpayer his 2009 appeal should not have been heard; and WHEREAS , the County Tax Board on October 29, 2009 erroneously issued a Judgment reducing the 2009 assessment to $76,700 (Land-$20,000, Bldg.-$56,700); and WHEREAS , the Township refused to honor the aforesaid Judgment since 2009 real property taxes had not been paid; and WHEREAS , on November 210, 2009, all delinquent real estate taxes were made current; and WHEREAS , the assessment on the subject property was never reduced to reflect the reduced assessment of $76,700; and WHEREAS , in 2009 and 2010 the property owner overpaid real property taxes computed on an erroneous assessment of $86,700 thus entitling him to a refund for 2009 and 2010; and WHEREAS , legal counsel has advised that the property owner should be reimbursed for any overpaid taxes paid in 2009 and 2010; and WHEREAS , the Tax Collector has advised that there is due and owing the property owner the following refunds for overpaid taxes: 2009 - $ 1,254.70 2010 - $1,298.20 NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED as follows: 1. The Township shall refund to the property owner all overpaid 2009 and 2010 real property taxes as set forth above. 2. The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector be and they are hereby authorized to adjust their records accordingly. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: May 17, 2011

119-11 May 31, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, JAMES K. & BETH A. GREENBERG are the owners of the real property and dwelling house at 9 Elm Court Way (Block 101.02, Lot 4); and WHEREAS, the subject property was formerly assessed as follows: LAND: $ 71,000.00 BLDG.: $279,300.00 $350,300.00 and WHEREAS , on April 16, 2010, the Tax Court of New Jersey entered Judgment reducing the assessment on the subject to $265,000.00 (Land - $71,000.00, Bldg.- $194,000); and WHEREAS , the assessment on the subject property should have been changed to $265,000.00 for tax year 2010 in order to reflect the Judgment entered on April 16, 2010 and to also comply with the “Freeze Act”; and WHEREAS, because of the aforesaid error the property owners overpaid the 2010 real property taxes which were erroneously calculated on an erroneous assessment of $350,300.00; and WHEREAS , legal counsel has advised that any overpaid 2010 real property taxes should be refunded to the property owner; and WHEREAS , the Council believes it would be in the best interest of the Township to refund any overpaid taxes; and WHEREAS , the Tax Collector has advised that there should be refunded to the property owners the sum of $10,074.50 representing all overpaid real property taxes for 2010. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that: 1. JAMES K. & BETH A. GREENBERG be refunded the sum of $10,074.50 which represents all overpaid 2010 real property taxes. 2. The Tax Collector & Tax Assessor be and they are authorized to adjust their records accordingly. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: May 17, 2011

1 18 -11 Ma y 17 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of May 17 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. ( X ) 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

Personnel Health Department Litigation NJ DEP, et al. v. Occidental Chemical Corp., et al. The Renna House (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on Ma y 17 , 2011. Motion: Joe Krakoviak Second: Patty Spango Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: May 17 , 2011

pages.text: 117-11 May 17, 2011 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING A WINDOW CONTRACT FOR COMPUTER EQUIPMENT AND INSTALLATION WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.4 et seq., when the cost of goods and/or services are under the Township’s bid threshold but exceed $17,500.00 a resolution to approve that the contract is compliant with the New Jersey Local Unit Pay To Play Laws; and WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange Administration and Finance Departments need to replace twelve co mputers, a server, and related software after nine years of service; and WHEREAS, the Purchasing Agent did receive quotes for this equipment and recommends the following company: Doctor Computer, LLC, 21 Ridgewood Drive, Livingston, NJ 07039 for 26,008.00 to be the most advantageous quote for cost and service ; and WHEREAS , the above named business or businesses have completed and submitted a Business Entity Disclosure Certification which certifies the business entity has not made any reportable contributions to a political or candidate committee in the Township of West Orange in the previous one year, and that the contract will prohibit the above named vendors from making any reportable contributions through the term of the contract. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Business Disclosure Entity Certification be on file with this resolution and will be published in accordance with the A pplicable law. Karen J. 1 115-11 May 17, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , on August 29, 2010, a fire was reported inside the Dollar Tree store located within the Township of West Orange (the “Township”), West Orange Plaza shopping center located at 235 Prospect Avenue, West Orange, New Jersey, 07052 (the “Property”); and WHEREAS , when the fire occurred, no alarm was activated; and WHEREAS , Township Fire Department and Police Department personnel responded to the fire; and WHEREAS , subsequent to the fire, Township fire officials reviewed and inspected the fire suppression and alarm equipment within and around the Dollar Tree; and WHEREAS, the Dollar Tree store and twelve (12) other stores within the Property are linked to one main fire protection system through, among other things, a series of standpipes and risers within the K-Mart store at the Property; and WHEREAS , Telgian Corporation (“Telgian” ) is a fire alarm system testing and inspection company which operates in the State of New Jersey ; and WHEREAS, K-Mart is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sears Holdings Corporation (“Sears”), a retail corporation, and is thus overseen by Sears; and WHEREAS , Telgian was the entity hired by Sears to oversee the fire alarm system within and around the K-Mart store at the Property ; and WHEREAS , upon inspection of the Property subsequent to the fire, and review of fire system inspection reports prepared by Telgian on or about March 10, 2009 and June 15, 2010, thirteen (13) Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty were issued by the Township Fire Department to Telgian, and were provided to Telgian by letter dated October 13, 2010; and WHEREAS , the Township provided Sears with five (5) Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty, via hand delivery of same to a K-Mart store manager; and WHEREAS , the Township cited Telgian and Sears for violations of the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code, specifically N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.12(b)9(i), for filing with the Township false statements of prior fire safety inspections, and N.J.A.C. 5:70-3.907.15 for failure to

2 properly maintain the fire safety system within and around the Dollar Tree, K-Mart store, and adjacent properties; and WHEREAS , Telgian appealed the thirteen (13) Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty to the Township’s Construction Board of Appeals, by way of appeals dated October 29, 2010; and WHEREAS, the Township Attorney’s office worked to resolve the issues between the Township, Telgian, and Sears; and WHEREAS , the Township, Telgian, and Sears have agreed to a mutual release and settlement of the claims arising out of the Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty issued to Telgian and Sears, with Telgian agreeing to concurrently withdraw and dismiss its appeals to the Township’s Construction Board of Appeals ; and NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED , by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, that in consideration of the mutual benefits conferred in the settlement agreement between the Township, Sears and Telgian, and subject to the terms and conditions stated therein, the Township is authorized to resolve the Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty as issued against Telgian and Sears, upon the execution of the settlement agreement; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, that the mutual release and settlement between the Township, Telgian and Sears is approved and shall be executed by the Mayor ; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED , that a true copy of this Agreement remain on file with the Township Clerk for inspection by the public. Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: May 17, 2011

(“Apex”) is a fire sprinkler subcontractor which operates in the State of New Jersey, and is the entity charged with overseeing the fire sprinkler system within the K-Mart store; and WHEREAS , upon inspection of the Property subsequent to the fire, and review of fire inspection reports submitted to the Township by Apex in or about December 2009, the Township Fire Department issued thirteen (13) Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty to Apex, six (6) notices having been received by Apex on or about September 15, 2010, and an additional seven (7) notices having been received by Apex on or about September 27, 2010; and WHEREAS , the Township cited Apex for violations of the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code, specifically N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.12(b)9(i) for the filing of false statements of its prior inspections, and N.J.A.C. 5:70-3.907.15 for failure to properly maintain the fire safety system within and around the Dollar Tree store and adjacent properties; and WHEREAS , Apex appealed the thirteen (13) Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay

2 Penalty to the Township’s Construction Board of Appeals, by way of appeals dated September 30, 2010 and October 12, 2010; and WHEREAS, the Township Attorney ’s office and Fire Official worked to resolve the issues between the Township and Apex; and WHEREAS , the Township and Apex have agreed to enter into a mutual release andsettlement of all claims, with Apex agreeing to withdraw and dismiss its appeals to the Township’s Construction Board of Appeals and any other appeals ; and NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED, by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, that in consideration of the mutual benefits conferred in the settlement agreement between the Township and Apex, and subject to the terms and conditions stated therein, the Township is authorized to resolve the Notices of Violation and Orders to Pay Penalty as issued against Apex ; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, that the mutual release and settlement between the Township and Apex is approved and shall be executed by the Mayor ; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a true copy of this Agreement remain on file with the Township Clerk for inspection by the public. 102-11 Ma y 3 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of May 3 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. () 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. ( X ) 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

Contract Negotiations Contract Negotiations with Police & Fire (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on Ma y 3 , 2011. Motion: Susan McCartney Second: Patty Spango Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: May 3 , 2011

and WHEREAS, on April 7, 2008, the Township of West Orange approved the “Harvard Press Redevelopment Plan” , which includes the property located at 22-24 Central Avenue, West Orange; and WHEREAS, on March 11, 2009 a Hazardous Discharge Site Remediation Fund application was submitted to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection ; and WHEREAS, the anticipated term of this contract is for one year ; and Whereas, by letter dated June 16, 2010, TRC Environmental Corporation, with offices located at 57 East Willow Street, Millburn, New Jersey, indicated that they could provide the required environmental engineering consulting services for an amount not to exceed $40,910; and WHEREAS, the engineering services to be provided by TRC Environmental Corporation are professional services and thus exempt from public bidding pursuant to the Local Public Contracts Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-1 et seq. ; pages.text: 79 - 11 March 29 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of March 29 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. ( X ) 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

L itigation City of Orange Tax Appeal Organon Tax Appeal Personnel Police Uniform Allowance (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on March 29 , 2011. Motion: Joe Krakoviak Second: Patty Spango Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: March 29 , 2011

The bonds referred to in Section 1 hereof are hereby combined into one consolidated issue of bonds in the aggregate principal amount of $11,505,000 and are sometimes hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Bonds.” The bonds referred to in subsections A through II of Section 1 shall each be designated “General Improvement Bonds, Series 2011” and shall be numbered with the prefix G from one consecutively upward. The bonds referred to in subsection JJ of Section 1 shall each be designated “Tax Appeal Refunding Bonds, Series 2011”

The bonds of said consolidated issue shall be dated the date of delivery and will be issued in fully registered form. When issued, the Bonds will be registered in the name of and held by Cede & Co., as the owner thereof and nominee for The Depository Trust Company, New York, New York (“DTC”), an automated depository for securities and clearinghouse for securities transactions. Upon issuance, the Bonds will be delivered to DTC in single denominations for each maturity of the General Improvement Bonds, Series 2011 and the Tax Appeal Refunding Bonds, Series 2011. Individual purchases of beneficial interests in the Bonds will be made in book-entry form (without certificates) in the denomination of $ 5 ,000 each or any integral multiple thereof. Principal of the Bonds will be paid annually, subject to prior optional redemption, on the first day of May in the following years and in the following aggregate amounts : $11,275,000 General Improvement Bonds, Series 2011, maturing in the principal amount of $425,000 in the year 2012; $500,000 in the year 2013; $550 ,000 in the year 2014; $750,000 in the year 2015; $800,000 in each of the years 2016 to 2021, inclusive; and $850,000 in each of the years 2022 to 2026, inclusive . $230,000 Tax Appeal Refunding Bonds, Series 2011, maturing in the principal amount of $230,000 in the year 2012. The Bonds maturing on or after May 1, 2022 shall be subject to redemption prior to their respective maturity dates, on or after May 1, 2021 at the option of the Township, either in whole or in part at any time in any order of maturity at one hundred percent (100%) of the principal amount of the Bonds being redeemed (the “Redemption Price”), plus in each case accrued interest thereon to the date fixed for redemption. Notice of Redemption shall be given by publishing such notice once a week for two (2) successive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation that carries financial news, is printed in the English language and is customarily published on each business day in the State of New York, the first of such publications to be at least thirty (30) but not more than sixty (60) days before the date fixed for redemption. A Notice of Redemption shall also be mailed by first class mail in a sealed envelope with postage prepaid to the registered owners of such Bonds at their respective addresses as they last appear on the registration books kept for that purpose by the Township. However, so long as DTC (or any successor thereto) acts as Securities Depository for the Bonds, Notices of Redemption shall be sent to such depository and shall not be sent to the beneficial owners of the Bonds, nor shall the notice be published as provided herein. Any failure of such depository to advise any of its participants or any failure of any participant to notify any beneficial owner of any Notice of Redemption shall not affect the validity of the redemption proceedings. If the Township determines to redeem a portion of the Bonds of a maturity, such Bonds shall be selected by the Township by lot. If Notice of Redemption has been given as described herein, the Bonds, or the portion thereof called for redemption, shall be due and payable on the date fixed for redemption at the Redemption Price, together with accrued interest to the date fixed for redemption. It is hereby found, determined and declared that the average period of usefulness of the improvements or purposes for which the said General Improvement Bonds are to be issued, taking into consideration the amount of such General Improvement Bonds to be issued for said improvements or purposes, is 15.08 years. It is hereby found, determined and declared that the period of usefulness of the improvements or purposes for which the said Tax Appeal Refunding Bonds are to be issued, taking into consideration the amount of such Tax Appeal Refunding Bonds to be issued for said improvements or purposes, is 1 year. Section 4. The Bonds shall bear interest from their date based on their outstanding principal amount at a rate to be determined as hereinafter set forth in Section 6 of this Resolution, shall be payable as to principal in lawful money of the United States of America at the administration office of the Township in West Orange, New Jersey, payable semi-annually on the first day of May and November in each year until maturity, commencing on November 1, 2011, by check or draft mailed on such interest payment date to the owners thereof registered as such as of each next preceding April 15 and October 15. Interest on the Bonds shall be calculated on the basis of a 360- day year of twelve 30-day calendar months. Notwithstanding any other provision herein to the contrary, so long as DTC or its nominee, Cede & Co., is the registered owner of the Bonds, payments of the principal of and interest on the Bonds will be made directly to Cede & Co., as nominee of DTC in accordance with the provisions of the DTC Letter of Representations to be executed by the Township and DTC. Disbursal of such payments to the DTC participants is the responsibility of DTC, and disbursal of such payments to the beneficial owners of the bonds is the responsibility of the DTC participants. Section 5. The Bonds shall be signed by the Mayor or Deputy Mayor and the Township Chief Financial Officer, by their manual or facsimile signatures, and the corporate seal of the Township shall be affixed thereto, or imprinted or reproduced thereon and shall be attested by the manual or facsimile signature of the Clerk or Deputy Clerk of the Township . Section 6. The Township Chief Financial Officer is hereby authorized and directed to take all actions necessary to offer the Bonds for public sale upon the submission of electronic proposals in accordance with all applicable statutes and to determine in his discretion the date for receipt for such proposals, all in accordance with the terms set forth in the Notice of Sale. The Township Chief Financial Officer is further hereby authorized and delegated the authority to sell and award the Bonds in accordance with the terms of the Notice of Sale and directed to report in writing to the Township Council at the next meeting succeeding the date when any sale or delivery of the Bonds pursuant to this resolution is made, such report to include the principal amount, description, interest rate and maturities of the Bonds sold, the price obtained and the name of the purchaser. The “Notice of Sale” shall comply in all respects with the applicable statutes relating thereto and shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A, with such additions, modifications or deletions as determined by the Township Chief Financial Officer. The Notice of Sale shall be published in a newspaper published and circulated in the Township as the Township Chief Financial Officer may select and a summary of the Notice of Sale shall be published in The Bond Buyer at least once at least seven (7) days prior to the date of public sale. The Township Chief Financial Officer is authorized and delegated the authority to postpone a public sale without readvertisement in accordance with all applicable statutes relating thereto. The obligations hereunder to pay for and to accept delivery of the Bonds shall be further conditioned on the availability and delivery to the Successful Bidder, at the time of delivery of the Bonds, of (i) certificates from the Township Chief Financial Officer in form satisfactory to Bond Counsel evidencing the proper execution and delivery of the Bonds, the receipt of payment therefor and the fact the Bonds will not be arbitrage obligations within the meaning of the Code; (ii) a certificate from the Township Attorney, in form and tenor satisfactory to Bond Counsel and dated as of the date of such delivery, to the effect that there is no litigation pending or (to the knowledge of the signer or signers thereof) threatened affecting the validity of the Bonds; and (iii) a certificate from the Township Chief Financial Officer, in form and tenor satisfactory to Bond Counsel and dated as of the date of such delivery, to the effect that to the best of his knowledge of such and belief, and after reasonable investigation: (1) neither the Official Statement relating to the Bonds nor any amendment, or supplement thereto contains any untrue statement of a material fact or omits to state any material fact necessary to make the statements therein, in the light of the circumstances in which they were made, not misleading; (2) since the date of the Official Statement (or the date of the most recent amendment or supplement thereto) no event has occurred which would make the statements therein untrue or, in the light of the circumstances in which they were made, misleading, and (3) there has not been any material adverse change in the operation or financial affairs of the Township since the date of such Official Statement. Concerning The Preliminary Official Statement The Township has issued an Official Statement with respect to the sale of the Bonds in preliminary form (the “Preliminary Official Statement”) which the Township has deemed final as of its date for purposes of paragraph (b)(1) of Rule 15c2-12 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Rule 15c2-12”), except for certain omissions permitted thereunder and except for changes permitted by other applicable law. The Preliminary Official Statement may be accessed via the Internet at www.i- dealprospectus.com. A printed version is also available upon request made to the Chief Financial Officer of the Township at the Municipal Building, 66 Main Street, West Orange, New Jersey 07052 (telephone (9 73 ) 325 - 4070 ). Official Statement The Township agrees to provide the successful bidder with up to two hundred (200) copies of the final Official Statement adopted by the Township in relation to the sale by the Township of the Bonds within the period of time allowed under Rule 15c2-12, at the sole cost and expense of the Township, with any additional copies which the successful bidder shall reasonably request to be provided at the sole cost and expense of the successful bidder. Continuing Disclosure In order to assist the successful bidder in complying with Rule 15c2-12, the Township agrees to deliver on the Closing Date a Continuing Disclosure Certificate to be dated as of the Closing Date pursuant to which the Township shall agree to provide at the times and to the information repositories and

72-11 March 29, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange entered into a contract with All State Technology, Inc., with offices at 10 Lark Lane, Oak Ridge, New Jersey 07438 for the Restoration of the Ginny Duenkel Municipal Pool Surfaces in the amount of $112,000.00; and WHEREAS, during the course of construction and the removal of the existing plaster surface on the main pool, the Township and the contractor discovered the caulking compound on the three main expansion joints had deteriorated; and WHEREAS, the Bid Specifications only required the expansion joints to be replastered; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer and Township Architect determined at all three expansion joints, the old and deteriorated caulking compound needs to be removed, the expansion joints cleaned and the expansion joints recaulked; and WHEREAS, to facilitate the maintenance of the expansion joints, the Township Engineer and Township Architect recommend a tile border be placed along the edges of the expansion joints and that the new plaster surface abut the outside edge of the border tile and not cover the expansion joint as previously existed; and WHEREAS, All State Technology, Inc. provided a price for this work of $4,530.00 or $30.00 per linear foot for the expansion joint length of 151 feet; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated March 23, 2011 recommends Change Order No 1 in the amount of $4,530.00 for this work to be performed by All State Technology, Inc.; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that Change Order No. 1 in the amount of $4,530.00 for the contract The Restoration of the Ginny Duenkel Municipal Pool Surfaces with All State Technology, Inc., 10 Lark Lane, Oak Ridge, New Jersey 07438 which represents a 4.04 percent increase in the contract amount be approved. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: March 29, 2011

71-11 March 29, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , there exists a need in the Township for medical assistance to review and sign off on certain medical-related governmental forms, and attend to and/or assess the health and/or injuries of Township personnel, including but not limited to Police Department employees, Fire Department employees, and other departments and non uniform personnel; WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange desires to appoint a Medical Director for the Township for the benefit of its employees and residents; WHEREAS , Dr. Anthony Quartell, a resident of the Township, has represented his interest and ability to serve as Medical Director for the Township at the salary of $1,000 per year; WHEREAS, Dr. Quartell is a medical doctor who possesses any and all required Board Certifications and the requisite skills and abilities to serve as Medical Director; WHEREAS, the cost to the Township falls below the threshold established by the Local Public Contracts Law, allowing the Township to contract for the services of a Medical Director without an open procurement process, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-3; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED, by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, that Dr. Anthony Quartell is hereby authorized to become the Township’s Medical Director and to administer certain medical services in exchange for a salary of $1,000 per year for any such services rendered. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by Township Council of the Township of West Orange, New Jersey as follows: 1. The contract for the performance of medical assistance, medical attendance to and/or medical assessments of the health and/or injuries of Township personnel, including but not limited to Police Department employees, Fire Department employees, and other departments and non uniform personnel is hereby awarded to Dr. Anthony Quartell. Dr. Anthony Quartell agrees that he shall serve as the Medical Director for the Township of West Orange which shall include the following responsibilities: (a) Reviewing, authorizing, and/or signing any and all required or requested administrative governmental forms or other documents in connection with the medical business or needs of the Township or its personnel and/or employees; (b) Will provide the supervision and authorization of State mandated medical services and the writing of necessary Health Department Standing Orders; and (c) Evaluating, when requested, the health and/or condition of certain Township personnel and/or employees, or other such individuals in his or the Township’s discretion.

2. Reimbursement of Expenses. Dr. Anthony Quartell shall receive reimbursement for out-of-pocket expenses up to a maximum of $50 per month during the contract period upon submission of receipts for necessary and approved supplies. All additional expenses above the $50 maximum will require the prior approval of the Township’s Business Administrator. 3. Independent Contractor. Dr. Anthony Quartell is an independent contractor who shall be solely responsible for his own work hours and daily responsibilities. As an independent contractor, Dr. Anthony Quartell shall be fully responsible for all obligations to any taxing authority or other governmental entity. Dr. Anthony Quartell shall receive no monetary or other benefits not specifically enumerated in this agreement. 4. Insurance. Dr. Anthony Quartell shall maintain all necessary insurance coverage to practice medicine, including but not limited to malpractice insurance. 5. Dr. Anthony Quartell shall be paid for the services set forth in this agreement the sum of $83.33 per month effective March 1, 2011 and continuing each month thereafter with the Township and Dr. Anthony Quartell having the right to terminate this agreement on five (5) days written notice at any time. 6. A copy of this Resolution shall be published in accordance with the law. 7. A copy of this Resolution shall be maintained on file with the Municipal Clerk available for public inspection. Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: March 29, 2011 ATTEST: TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE By: Karen J. Carnevale Mayor Robert D. Parisi Township Clerk ACCEPTED: DR. ANTHONY QUARTELL By : Anthony Quartell, M.D.

documents.title: TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION

pages.text: 56 - 11 March 8 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of March 8 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. ( X ) 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

Personnel Harassment Investigation Contract Negotiations with Police & Fire L itigation Holland v. TOWO (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on March 8 , 2011. Motion: Joe Krakoviak Second: Patty Spango Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: March 8 , 2011

53-11 March 8, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , there exists in the Township of West Orange, a need for the services of a firm or individual specializing in the investigation, research, planning, preparation and pursuit of grants and other programs submitted to various County, State and Federal authorities and foundations for obtaining vital financial and other aid for municipal programs; and WHEREAS, such services involve professional knowledge and services as financial advisors pertaining to grants as well as specialized knowledge of available County, State and Federal aid programs and corporate and private foundations and the preparation of applications, submissions and actions necessary to obtain and successfully pursue such programs ; and WHEREAS, the need for such services is great and immediate and the necessary funds are available; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange has prepared a Request for Qualifications for Professional Services; and WHEREAS , the Township has received a response from Alicia Skinner trading as Skinn er Consulting Services (“Alicia Skinner”); and WHEREAS , the Township seeks to retain Alicia Skinner to fulfill this need for a six (6) month period at the rate of $ 14 ,000, commencing March 1 , 20 11 and ending August 31 , 20 11 ; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by Township Council of the Township of West Orange, New Jersey as follows: 1. The contract for the performance of all necessary professional consultation and work involved in the study of County, State, Federal corporate and private aid funds needs of the Township of West Orange, New Jersey, and the related research, planning, preparation, submission and proceeding with all applications and programs for such programs is hereby awarded to Alicia Skinner. Alicia Skinner agrees that new grants (“New Grants”) of at least the amount paid to it will be obtained during the term of this agreement and agrees that it will continue

2 to provide services beyond the term of this agreement at no cost until New Grants exceeding the amount received are awarded. This amount specifically excludes all currently existing grants. 2. Reimbursement of Expenses. Alicia Skinner shall receive reimbursement for out- of-pocket expenses up to a maximum of $50 per month during the contract period upon submission of receipts for necessary and approved supplies including ink cartridges, postage and related items. 3. Independent Contractor. Alicia Skinner is an independent contractor who shall be solely responsible for her own work hours and daily responsibilities. As an independent contractor, Alicia Skinner shall be fully responsible for all obligations to any taxing authority or other governmental entity. Alicia Skinner shall receive no monetary or other benefits not specifically enumerated in this agreement. 4. New Grants. New Grants shall be defined as receipt of monies not previously received by the Township during the past five (5) years. 5. All grant applications are subject to the approval of the Township in its sole discretion. No grant application shall be submitted without the approval of the Township Council. 6. Reporting. Alicia Skinner shall submit a written report to the Mayor and Council concerning all services rendered and new grants obtained on a quarterly basis. In addition, Alicia Skinner shall attend any meetings requested by the Mayor and/or Business Administrator to discuss potential grants and report as to timetables for submission of grant applications, status of grant applications, and areas of available grant funds. 7. Alicia Skinner shall be paid for the services set forth in this agreement the sum of $2,333.33 per month effective March 1, 2011 and continuing each month thereafter with the Township and Alicia Skinner having the right to terminate this agreement on five (5) days written notice at any time .

3 8. A copy of this Resolution shall be published in accordance with the law. 9. A copy of the Resolution shall be maintained on file with the Municipal Clerk available for public inspection. ________________________________ Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. pages.text: 44-11 March 8, 2011 TONNAGE GRANT APPLICATION RESOLUTION WHEREAS, The Mandatory Source Separation and Recycling Act, P.L.1987, c.102, has established a recycling fund from which tonnage grant may be made to municipalities in order to encourage local source separation and recycling programs; and WHEREAS, It is the intent and the spirit of the Mandatory Source Separation and Recycling Act to use the tonnage grants to develop new municipal recycling programs and to continue and to expand existing programs; and WHEREAS, The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection has promulgated recycling regulations to Implement the Mandatory Source Separation and Recycling Act; and WHEREAS, The recycling regulations impose on municipalities certain requirements as a condition for applying for tonnage grants, including but not limited to, making and keeping accurate, verifiable records of materials collected and claimed by the municipality; and WHEREAS, A resolution authorizing this municipality to apply for the 2010 Recycling Tonnage Grant will memorialize the commitment of this municipality to recycling and to indicate the assent of the Township Council to the efforts undertaken by the municipality and the requirements contained in the Recycling Act and recycling regulations; and WHEREAS, Such a resolution should designate the individual authorized to ensure the application is properly completed and timely filed. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange hereby endorses the submission of the recycling tonnage grant application to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection and designates Nick Salese, R ecycling C oordinator to ensure that the application is properly filed; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the monies received from the recycling tonnage grant be deposited in a dedicated recycling trust fund to be used solely for the purposes of recycling. KAREN J. CARNEVALE, MUNICIPAL CLERK SAL M. ANDERTON, COUNCIL PRESIDENT Adopted: March 8, 2011

pages.text: 38- 11 February 22 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of February 22 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. ( X ) 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

Personnel Contract Negotiations -Police & Fire Litigation Seton Hall Prep (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on February 22 , 2011. Motion: Patty Spango Second: Sal Anderton Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: February 22, 2011

21-11 February 8, 2011 GOOSE CONTROL TECHNOLOGY A Division of Animal Damage Control Systems Inc. SERVICE AGREEMENT - CAL E NDER YEAR 2011 THIS AGREEMENT is made as of March_____, 2011 The Township of West Orange (Client) whose address is 66 Main Street West Orange, NJ 07052 and Goose Control Technology (Consultant/Contractor) In consideration of the mutual covenants contained in this agreement, Client and Contractor agree as follows: 1. Services. Consultant agrees to provide Client with the services necessary to legally abate and control nuisance-related Canada Geese problems on the subject property located at (all municipal park properties). Contractor agrees to perform such services under the terms and c onditions set forth in this contract. 2. Compliance with Law. Consultant shall be responsible for obtaining a permit, on behalf of the Client, from the United States Fish and Wildlife Service ("USFWS"), or any other state or local permitting authority, if required. Said permit(s) shall authorize the Client as the permit holder, to engage in the lawful control, management and/or removal of Canada Geese located on the Property. Upon the issuance of the permit(s), Client shall be solely responsible for the permit(s) and shall keep same on the Premises at all times. Contractor will provide all relevant records and information necessary for Client to maintain the permit(s) and ensure compliance of same. Consultant's failure to obtain said permit(s) on behalf of the Client for reasons beyond the control of the Consultant shall not be deemed a breach of the terms and conditions of this Contract, but this agreement shall terminate and Consultant shall promptly return any fee received. 3. Duties. Contractor agrees to perform any and all services, pursuant to the terms of the permit(s) and all applicable federal, state and local regulatory guidelines, necessary to reduce and or eliminate the Canada Geese population from the subject Property. These services may include harvest management programs, habit management programs, hazing/harassment programs, nest treatment and, if deemed appropriate, removal and lawful disposal of Canada Geese. Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials and personnel necessary to facilitate any and all of these services. Upon Consultant's on-site evaluation, the parties agree that the specific services to be provided in this Contract are as follows: Egg treatment @ 3 sites (eggs to be oiled) $ 2,500 Permit facilitation/record keeping – no fee Volunteer Management for nest identification - $ 500 4. Term. The duration of this Agreement shall be for one year commencing on the date of execution , or as the parties to this Agreement shall otherwise agree. 5. Compensation. As compensation for the services performed under this Agreement, the Client shall pay Contractor the total sum of $3,000.00 for permit processing and egg treatment, and volunteer management. Fifty percent (50%) of which shall be paid upon the execution of this Agreement and the balance upon completion of services.

6. Access and Security. Client agrees that Consultant shall have reasonable access to the Property for the purpose of performing such services as described herein. Client agrees to provide the security necessary to enable Contractor to perform its services and shall take all reasonable steps to prevent any interference by third parties in the abatement program. In the event that the Contractor cannot perform its services as a result of third party interference and through no fault of either party, Contractor shall be entitled to payment of one-half of the total sum of compensation due under the contract as provided in paragraph 5 of this Agreement. 6. Force Majeure. Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement, neither party shall be liable to the other for failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement due to fire, flood, strikes, or other industrial disturbances, accidents, war, acts of God or other causes beyond the reasonable control of the parties including changes in the law concerning Canada Geese control and abatement activities. 7. Warranties and Representations . Contractor agrees to provide conscientious, competent and diligent services and will take all reasonable and lawful steps to effectively abate the nuisance-causing geese. However, Contractor does not and cannot warrant any result or final outcome for the services that it performs herein. 8. Relationship of Parties. The parties intend that Contractor, in performing services specified in this Agreement, shall act as an independent contractor and shall have control of its work and the manner in which it is performed. Contractor shall be free to contract for similar services to be performed for other employers while Contractor is under contract with the Client. Contractor is not to be considered an agent or employee of Client and is not entitled to participate in any pension plans, bonus, stock, or similar benefits that Client may provide for its employees. 9. Liability. Contractor shall take all precautions necessary for the safety of and prevention of damage to property on the Property and for the safety of and prevention of injury to persons, including Client's employees, Contractor's employees and third persons, on the Property. All work shall be performed entirely at Contractor's risk. Contractor agrees to carry, for the duration of this contract, public liability insurance in an amount, and with an insurer, acceptable to Client. Consultant shall name the Client as an additional insured on any insurance policies in place. Consultant also agrees to release, indemnify and hold harmless the Client from any losses for bodily injury and/or property damage, including attorneys fees and expenses, arising out of or in any manner resulting from the services to be performed by the Consultant. CANADA GOOSE REPRODUCTION CONTROL VOLUNTEER PROGRAM Township of West Orange Amendment 1 Introduction – The proposal presented below is the result an ongoing nuisance goose control program at the sites(s). The proposal is directed at the elimination of existing Canada goose reproduction utilizing the assistance of the Township of West Orange volunteers. Recruitment, management and training of volunteers – The recruitment of volunteers who participate in the reproduction control program shall be the responsibility of the Township of West Orange, and shall be limited to no more then 20 volunteers. Volunteers during their participation in the program shall be considered employees of the Township of West Orange. On site management and training of volunteers shall be the responsibility of Goose Control Technology of NJ Inc. Media relations – All press releases, or other interaction with the media related to this program shall be subject to the review and approval of both the Township of West Orange and Goose Control Technology of NJ Inc . Volunteer Identification and Supplies - The Township of West Orange shall provide each participating volunteer with identification it deems needed, as well as all materials and supplies needed to mark nest sites and test eggs. Volunteer Duties - Participating volunteer activities will be limited to the identification of Canada goose nest sites and the testing of egg viability. Volunteers will not treat eggs. This shall be done only by Goose Control Technology staff using oil. Volunteer work schedules, reporting and on-site activities shall be as directed by Goose Control Technology of NJ, Inc. Separation from the Volunteer Program – Volunteers participating in the program serves at the pleasure of the Township of West Orange. Failure to comply with the guidelines presented in this proposal may result in separation from the program. Duration of Services – Goose Control Technology will provide the services described in this proposal for a one-year period. Approved by_________________________ Goose Control Technology of NJ , Inc.
