20-11 February 8, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange (the “Township”) issued a Request for Bid Proposal for Janitorial Services (the “RFP”) at several municipal buildings including West Orange Town Hall, West Orange Police Building, West Orange Senior Health Center, Department of Public Works/Engineering, Department of Recreation, West Orange Police Valley Road, and West Orange Police Washington Street Sub Station ; and WHEREAS, on December 21, 2010, the Township received two (2) bids in response to the RFP: (1) Ocean Clean from Cedar Grove, New Jersey with a bid price of $55,692 and (2) Excellent Building Services Corp. from Orange, New Jersey with a bid price of $57,540; and WHEREAS, the RFP required that each vendor provide its experience and qualification as provided in the Bidder’s Requirements Check List; and WHEREAS, the Township advised that the basis of the award would include investigation of references provided by the vendor to determine the vendor’s ability to perform the work; and WHEREAS, the Proposal Form also required that each bidder provides an hourly rate for optional services including stripping and waxing floors; and WHEREAS, Ocean Clean failed to provide its experience and qualifications and failed to provide references with its bid; and WHEREAS, Ocean Clean also failed to provide an hourly rate, but instead provides a price per square feet for optional services; and WHEREAS, on December 28, 2010, Excellent Building Services, submitted an objection to Ocean Clean’s bid attacking Ocean Clean’s price per square foot for the optional services; and WHEREAS , under the New Jersey Supreme Court case of Meadowbrook Carting Company, Inc. v. Borough of Island Heights, 138 N.J. 307 (1994), Ocean Clean’s omission of references and listing of qualifications and experience and error as to the pricing for optional

services constitute material defects as they (1) deny the Township a means of comparing the bids under the basis outlined in the bid specifications and (2) deny the Township a means of checking references in order to determine whether Ocean Clean can properly perform the servi ces as well as pricing for optional services. See also Township of River Vale v. R.J. Longo Construction Co., Inc., 127 N.J. Super. 207 (Law Div. 1974). NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE that the bid submitted by Ocean Clean in response to the Township’s Request for Bid Proposal is hereby rejected as a materially defective bid; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Township shall award the contract for Janitorial Services to Excellent Building Services, Corp.; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Mayor be and is hereby authorized to execute all documents necessary to effectuate the Contract and the Municipal Clerk be and is hereby authorized to attest to the Mayor’s signature; and it is further RESOLVED, that the original of the Contract between Township of West Orange and Excellent Building Services, Corp. shall be maintained in the Municipal Clerk’s office. Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: February 8, 2011

pages.text: 15 -11 January 18 , 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of January 18 , 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. () 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

Holland v. Township of West Orange NJ DEP, et al. v. Occidental Chemical Corp., et al. Orange Reservoir Tax Appeal (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. 12-11 JANUARY 18, 2011 RESOLUTION Whereas, the Seton Hall Preparatory School (the “Seton Hall”) made application to the West Orange Zoning Board of Adjustment (“Zoning Board”) on various dates for site plan approval with variances to add additional playing fields and new structures on its premises off of Prospect Avenue, also known as Block 81.01, Lots 1.01, 1.04, 1.05 and 1.06 and Block 82.01, Lots 1, 7, 7.01, 7.02, and 7.05 (the “Subject Property”) and collectively (the “Application”); and WHEREAS, Seton Hall’s Application was heard at public meetings of the Zoning Board held on November 6, 2008, March 12, 2009, April 23, 2009, May 14, 2009, May 28, 2009, June 11, 2009, July 9, 2009, September 10, 2009, October 29, 2009, November 5, 2009, November 19, 2009, December 3, 2009, January 14, 2010, January 21, 2010, February 4, 2010, March 4, 2010, April 1, 2010, April 15, 2010, May 6, 2010, June 3, 2010, June 17, 2010, June 24, 2010, July 21, 2010, September 1, 2010, October 7, 20 10 , and November 8, 20 10 , and December 16, 2010 ; and WHEREAS, on November 8, 2010, the Zoning Board issued a decision granting the Application with variances and conditions ; and WHEREAS, on November 24, 2010, the Township Clerk for the Township of West Orange received from Herbert I. Waldman, Esq., of Javerbaum Wurgaft Hicks Kahn Wikstrom & Sinins, on behalf of Kevin Malanga, a Notice of Appeal to the Township Council pursuant toN.J.S.A. 40:55D-17 and Township of West Orange Ordinance 25:50-1 alleging that the “ Zonin g Board erroneously found that the intended use is an inherently beneficial use, that the Zoning Board erroneously found that the project’s benefits outweigh its detriments, that the Zoning Board failed to take into account the parking and safety issues relating to the site ” ; and WHEREAS, on November 29, 2010, the Township Clerk for the Township of West Orange received from Rhea Seagull, Ronni Strell, Barry Schustermann, and Loren Svetvilas (along with Kevin Malanga collectively referred to as “Appellants”) Notices of Appeal to the Township Council pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40:55D-17 and Township of West Orange Ordinance 25:50-1 alleging, among other things, that the “ Zoning Board erroneously found that the intended use is an inherently beneficial use, that the Zoning Board erroneously found that the project’s benefits outweigh its detriments, that the Zoning Board failed to take into sufficient account the flooding, parking and safety issues relating to the site, and that the decision was written with knowledge that it cannot be adequately enforced as the Township has insufficient means to support the legislature (the "Appeal") ” ; and WHEREAS, on December 16, 2010, the Zoning Board adopted Resolution ZB-08-37, the resolution memorializing the granting of site plan approval with variances and conditions to Seton Hall (the “Resolution”); and WHEREAS, the Resolution was published in the West Orange Chronicle on December 23, 2010 ; and WHEREAS, N.J.S.A. 40:55D-10(g) provides that the date of the adoption of the memorializing resolution constitutes the date of the decision for purposes of the mailings, filings, and publications required by law; and WHEREAS, N.J.S.A. 40:55D-17 (the “ MLUL ”) sets forth the procedures that govern an appeal made to the governing body following any final decision of a zoning board of adjustment approving an application for development pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40:55D-70(d); and

2 WHEREAS, the MLUL provides that an appeal is initiated by the filing of a Notice of A ppeal with the clerk of the municipality in which the board is located; and WHEREAS, the MLUL requires that within five (5) days of service of the Notice of Appeal the appellant must either (i) arrange for a transcript for use by the governing body and pay a deposit of $50.00 or the estimated cost of such transcript, whichever is less or (ii) within thirty five (35) days of service of the Notice of Appeal submit a transcript to the municipal clerk or the appeal may be dismissed by the governing body for failure to prosecute; and WHEREAS, the MLUL states that the governing body must make a review of the record below and issue a decision by no later than ninety five (95) days from the date of publication of the notice of the zoning board of adjustment’s decision or the governing body’s lack of action may be viewe d as a decision affirming the action of the zoning board of adjustment; and WHEREAS, at the meeting of the governing body all parties are afforded the opportunity to submit oral and written argument on the record ; and WHEREAS, per the MLUL the governing body may either reverse, remand or affirm with or without certain conditions the final decision of the zoning board of adjustment, however, an affirmative vote of a majority of the full authorized membership of the governing body shall be necessary to either reverse, remand to the zoning board of adjustment, to impose conditions on approval, or to alter conditions on approval, and once decided the governing body must adopt a resolution identify ing its findings and reasons for any disagreement; and WHEREAS, the Town Council for the Township of West Orange now desires to establish the procedures that will govern the instant A ppeals; NOW THERFORE, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange as follows: 1. Within five (5) days of service of the Notice of Appeal, or by no later than December 28, 2010 the Appellants shall either (a) pay a deposit and arrange for a transcript to be used by the governing body or (b) within thirty five (35) days of service of the Notice of Appeal, or by no later than February 4, 2011, submit a transcript to the Township Clerk. For economy of cost and to minimize copying, the Appellants shall scan the various transcripts from the hearings and place them on electronic discs and submit ten (10) copies of the discs to the Township Clerk. Appellants' submissions on the discs shall include any and all evidence submitted by Appellants to the Zoning Board. The Zoning Board shall provide all of Applicant's evidence. 2. The Township Council shall conduct its hearing on this appeal and issue its decision no later than ninety five (95) days after the date of publication of the notice of the Zoning Board’s decision, which was December 23, 2010. As such, the Township Council shall hold its hearing on Thursday, March 10, 2011 at 5:00 p.m. and Tuesday, March 15, 2011 at 5:00 p.m. (the “Hearing”). If needed, and at the sole discretion of the Township Council, the Hearing may be continued to another date. Thereafter, the Township Council shall deliberate and issue its decision by no later than March 25, 2011. 3. Thirty (30) days prior to the Hearing, or no later than February 7, 2011, Appellant may submit a brief or memorandum to the Township Council consisting of no more than twenty (20) pages setting forth his/her position with respect to the Appeal . 4. No later than February 21, 2011, Applicant may submit a brief or memorandum

3 to the Township Council consisting of no more than twenty (20) pages setting forth Applicant's position with respect to the Appeal. 5. During the Hearing, Appellant Malanga, represented by Mr. Waldman, shall have no more than thirty (30) minutes to present oral argument. Every other Appellant shall be afforded no more than fifteen (15) minutes to present oral argument. Applicant shall have thirty (30) minutes to present oral argument. The Township Council shall have the opportunity to ask any questions that it may have of any party. 6. Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40:55D-17, the Municipal Clerk shall forward copies of this Resolution via certified mail and regular postage prepaid to Appellants Rhea Seagull, 662 Prospect Avenue, West Orange, NJ 07052, Ronni Strell, 654 Prospect Avenue, West Orange, NJ 07052, Barry Schustermann, 21 Benvenue Avenue, West Orange, NJ 07052, Loren Svetvilas, 699 Prospect Avenue, West Orange, NJ 07052, Kevin Malanga, c/o Herbert I. Waldman, Esq., Javerbaum Wurgaft, Hicks, Kahn, Wikstrom & Sinins, 201 Washington Street, Newark, NJ 07102, and the Zoning Board at least ten (10) days prior to the date of the Township Council’s hearing on the appeal, or by no later than February 26, 2011. Additionally, the Municipal Clerk shall notice the Hearing in accordance with the Open Public Meetings Act, N.J.S.A. 10:4-6. The Municipal Clerk shall also provide a copy of this Resolution to the Director of Planning and the Zoning Board Attorney. KAREN J. CARNEVALE, MUNICIPAL CLERK SAL M. ANDERTON, COUNCIL PRESIDENT ADOPTED: JANUARY 18, 2011

07-11 January 18, 2011 RESOLUTION WHEREAS , the division of Alcoholic Beverages Control (ABC) is responsible for administering the Office of Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention (OJJDP) State Block Grant Program Enforcing the Underage Drinking Laws; and WHEREAS, The West Orange Police Department applied to ABC for funds in connection with a project entitled Cops-in-Shop Grant; and WHEREAS , the Township of West Orange Township Council had already reviewed the application and had deemed it to be in the best interests of the Township; and WHEREAS , the project is a joint project between the State of New Jersey (ABC) and the West Orange Department for the purpose of combating underage drinking; and WHEREAS , the State of New Jersey (ABC) has allocated a federal sub grant award in the amount of $ ___________ to the Township; and WHEREAS, there is no matching requirement by the Township. NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED , by the Township Council that the Township of West Orange wishes to participate with the State of New Jersey, Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) to the greatest extent possible; that the Township hereby approves and authorizes the execution of the sub grant award documentation; and that the Chief Financial Officer of the Township shall accept the funds in connection with the project from the ABC and make disbursements in accordance with said application. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED , that the Mayor and Chief of Police be and are hereby authorized to execute any and all documentation necessary to obtain the grant and effectuate the purposes set forth therein. A copy of the grant shall be available to the public upon request and in accordance with NJSA 47:1A-1 et seq. Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: January 18, 2011

06-11 January 18, 2011 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS , the construction firm Automatic Door Systems with offices at 86 Porete Avenue, North Arlington, New Jersey 07031 was awarded the contract for the construction of a new entrance canopy enclosure addition to the West Orange Police Facility in the amount of $104,850.00 for the Base Bid and $10,000.00 for Alternate No. 1 on April 27, 20 1 0; and WHEREAS , the construction period for the completion of this project was set at 210 calendar days from the “Notice to Proceed”, which was set at a period from June 1, 2010 to December 28, 2010; and WHEREAS , Automatic Door Systems was delayed for several reasons to miss their deadline to complete this project by December 28, 2010; and WHEREAS , the Engineering Department met with representatives of Automatic Door Systems to determine the period of construction delay recommended during the winter months; and WHEREAS , it was agreed by the respective parties to suspend construction until March 14, 2011 and set the new substantial completion date at June 12, 2011, which is a period of ninety (90) days; and WHEREAS , the firm of Automatic Door Systems agrees to perform the required work at no additional cost increase contained in the contract; and WHEREAS , the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the West Orange Township Council that the construction work on the new entrance canopy enclosure addition to the West Orange Police Facility be suspended from December 28, 2010 to March 13, 2011 and the work resumed on March 14, 2011 for ninety days until the new substantial completion date of June 12, 2011. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: January 18, 2011

documents.title: TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION

pages.text: 05-11 January 4, 2011 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS , the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS , prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS , this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED , that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of January 4, 2011 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2 . A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. ( X ) 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10 . Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ) :

West Essex Highlands Personnel-Employee Contracts (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED , that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on January 4, 2011. Motion: Victor Cirilo Second: Sal Anderton Vote Aye: 5 Opposed: 0 Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: January 4, 2011

02-1 1 January 4, 2011 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, J & S Construction Management of 405 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, N.J. 07052, J & S C.M.U. LLC of 322 Runnymead Road, Essex Fells, New Jersey 07021 and Stuart Dahan and Joseph Rolandelli as Principals collectively referred to as Developer were the prior owner and builder of a single family residence on Block 152.28, Lot 1271 commonly known as 2 Henry Street; and WHEREAS, the Developer as part of their Land Use Approval from the West Orange Planning Board and as part of the Municipal Land Use Law, N.J.S.A. 40:55D-1 et seq were required to make certain on site, off site and off tract improvements; and WHEREAS, at the time a Certificate of Occupancy was requested for the residence at 2 Henry Street some of the Developer’s obligations were incomplete; and WHEREAS, to secure the future performance of the Developer to complete these obligations a bond consisting of $2,811.00 in cash and a Surety Bond issued by Western Surety Company, Bond No. 70922793 in the amount of $28,110.00 was posted with the Township; and WHEREAS, the Certificate of Occupancy was issued with the requirement that the Developer complete all the improvements and obligations secured by the Performance Bond by October 30, 2010; and WHEREAS, the work to be performed by the Developer is not complete; and WHEREAS, the Municipal Engineer by letter dated December 1, 2010 advised CNA Surety as the agent for Western Surety Company that the obligations were not completed; and WHEREAS, CNA Surety by e-mail dated December 15, 2010 advised the Township that one of the principals Stewart Dahan advised CNA Surety that he intends to construct one of the obligations – the installation of a hot mix bituminous concrete base pavement; and WHEREAS, by letter dated December 22, 2010 from the Municipal Engineer to CNA Surety, CNA Surety was advised that over a month has passed since Mr. Dahan advised the

Township of his intentions; and WHEREAS, in the December 22, 2010 letter to CNA Surety, the Municipal Engineer advises CNA Surety he will request the Township Council find the Developers in default of their obligations secured by Western Surety Company Bond No. 70922793 for improvements associated with 2 Henry Street, Block 152.28, Lot 1271, and demand Western Surety Company complete all outstanding improvements; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that J & S Construction Management of 405 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, N.J. 07052, J & S C.M.U. LLC of 322 Runnymead Road, Essex Fells, New Jersey 07021 and Stuart Dahan and Joseph Rolandelli as Principals are found to be in default of their obligations to make certain on site, off site and off tract improvements associated with the development of 2 Henry Street, Block 152.28, Lot 1271 as required by the Land Use Approval of the West Orange Planning Board and the Municipal Land Use Law N.J.S.A. 40:55D-1 et seq. whose performance was guaranteed by Western Surety Company Bond No. 70922793. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange demands Western Surety Company complete the work secured by Bond No. 70922793. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that certified copies of this Resolution be sent by Certified Mail to J & S Construction Management of 405 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, N.J. 07052, J & S C.M.U. LLC of 322 Runnymead Road, Essex Fells, New Jersey 07021 and Stuart Dahan and Joseph Rolandelli. SAL M. ANDERTON, COUNCIL PRESIDENT KAREN J. CARNEVALE, MUNICIPAL CLERK Adopted: January 4, 2011

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED , that the Mayor and Township Council of the Township of West Orange adopt the attached cash management plan, including the official depositories for the Township of West Orange 'for the 2011 year. Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Municipal Clerk Council President Adopted: January 4, 2011
